rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=40, recon_eta=30.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, recon_dc_solver=cg, val_n=120, train_n=0, rationale=iter-6 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon — AUDIT CODE-FIX VALIDATION (user-directed 2026-06-20). ONE KNOB: recon_dc_solver legacy->cg (NEW config-gated correct DC path in solver_diffusion_recon.py; legacy path byte-for-byte preserved + reproducible for all prior cfgs). The audit found the legacy DC-step is (1) a MISLABELED steepest-descent dressed as CG (dc_step_cg lines ~83-100) and (2) a re-injection that recomputes x0 from a STALE eps via x0_from_eps(x,eps,ab_next) then re-noises with a FRESH randn mid-schedule (lines ~162-174) — this collapsed unconstrained iter-4 to SSIM 0.055 and kept the constrained variant stuck 0.24-0.66 << the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor at hr=0. THE FIX (ported from the corrected solver_fast_recon.cg_data_consistency): recon_dc_solver=cg swaps in a GENUINE Fletcher-Reeves CG solve of AtA x = At y (residual + conjugate direction + FR beta), forms x0 from the CURRENT step's eps (x0_hat at t_now, not a stale eps re-eval'd at the wrong alpha_bar), CG-projects it, then re-embeds at t_next DETERMINISTICALLY as sqrt(ab_next)*x0_proj_norm + sqrt(1-ab_next)*eps_pred reusing the SAME eps (eps-prediction => the level-t noise direction IS eps_pred) — NO fresh randn, NO stale eps. BASE = iter-5 BEST (T=40, eta=30, relax=1.0, every5/n_cg3/warmup5, val_n=120, SSIM 0.6647/hr0 — the run-best constrained config). Hard DC stays ON (recon_dcstep_every=5) now that it is CORRECT. HONEST EXPECTATION: the corrected CG-DC should STOP the legacy re-noise corruption and likely RAISE SSIM above iter-5's 0.6647 (the deterministic same-eps re-embed no longer overwrites the trajectory with fresh noise + a least-squares fit to the noisy 2304-view LD sinogram). But on DENSE rebinned Mayo (LD-FBP near-complete at 2304 views) the v4 DDPM prior is regime-bounded, so hr may STILL be ~0 — the real payoff is the 128-view SPARSE benchmarks + the planned EMA v5 prior. This iter VALIDATES the fix RUNS and is NON-REGRESSIVE/non-corrupting under the corrected metric. FALSIFIER: if SSIM drops below iter-5's 0.6647 the corrected re-embed is mis-scaling x0 vs eps; if it clears the ~0.81 FBP floor (hr>0) the legacy bug was the whole story. BUDGET: recon_dc_solver=cg is roughly cost-neutral vs legacy (the DPS forward+grad per step is unchanged; the CG inner loop does forward+back per n_cg, comparable to legacy dc_step_cg's forward+back+forward; the deterministic re-embed drops the randn). iter-5 ran T=40 x val_n=120 in 988.0 s = 16.5 min < the HARD 1200s/20-min budget (1800s in-solver backstop + 30-min --time). val_n=120 held at iter-5's value (no reduction needed — 988s leaves ~3.5 min headroom for the CG path's marginal delta). val=120 evenly-spaced L277, 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov=False). staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps single-val-ps probe, bg_target=truth, reuse ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt (NO retrain), 321px FOV.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=4, n_iter=18, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, lr=0.00015, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1080, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=dual_domain_n2i iter-6 (search-20260619-01, PER-IMAGE Noise2Inverse: warm-start pre-pass + per-scan Adam fit; NEVER amortized). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS, measured from iter-3/4/5 observations). (1) n_iter TRAJECTORY at anchored lr=3e-4, pretrain_epochs=4: iter-3 (n_iter=15) SSIM 0.9185, hr 0.1506, PSNR 35.50; iter-4 (n_iter=18) SSIM 0.9277, hr 0.19761 (BEST), PSNR 35.99, RMSE 7.934e-4, elapsed 1235.5s; iter-5 (n_iter=20, outer_wall 1150) SSIM 0.9169, hr 0.15949, PSNR 35.59, RMSE 8.310e-4 -- REGRESSED below iter-4. (2) LIMITER: hr is NOT monotone in n_iter -- it rose 15->18 then FELL 18->20. iter-5 falsifier TRIGGERED: n_iter past 18 OVERFITS each per-scan U-Net fit (PSNR fell 35.99->35.59, RMSE rose), exactly the confirmed campaign-wide insight that the per-scan U-Net N2I OVERFITS each scan and raising n_iter HURTS. n_iter is now MAPPED with an interior peak at 18. The confirmed correctly-signed lever for the overfit regime is per-scan lr-DOWN (anchor nearer the FBP-quality warm-start init): mayo-n2i 1e-3->3e-4 gave 0.9508->0.9541; lr has NEVER been pushed below 3e-4 in this campaign. ONE LIVE KNOB: tv_lambda 0.001->0.0005 (HALVE). The solver (solver_tv_iterative.py) reads ONLY tv_lambda/tv_iterations/tv_lr/tv_clip_max in tv_reconstruction(); tv_decay/tv_init/tv_optimizer are INERT (step decay is hard-coded 0.01). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, 120 iters unless noted): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.08) = BEST-at-120, #4 on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003) REGRESSED over-smoothed; iter-4 SSIM 0.926664 hr 0.208547 RMSE 7.825e-4 (iters 120->160, 1227.4s OVER WALL); iter-5 SSIM 0.926072 hr 0.187286 RMSE 8.036e-4 (lr 0.01->0.02, 971.8s) REGRESSED -- GD OVERSHOOT at the larger step (falsifier-branch a). LEVER MAP: clip exhausted (at top of bound [0.03,0.08]); lambda-UP regressed (iter-3); iters-UP plateaued +0.003hr AND breached wall (iter-4); lr-UP regressed via overshoot (iter-5). The ONLY untried direction on the only unexhausted lever is lambda-DOWN. FAILURE MODE: at lambda=0.001 the data term dominates but the TV penalty still lightly over-smooths real anatomy edges/bone; the RMSE-sensitive headroom metric penalizes that residual smoothing. HYPOTHESIS: halving tv_lambda 0.001->0.0005 weakens the TV penalty so the data term recovers finer edge/bone detail, dropping val_rmse below iter-2 7.857e-4 (the apples-to-apples 120-iter reference) so hr rises above iter-4 BEST 0.208547 at ZERO extra compute. FALSIFIER: if hr<=0.208547 (no gain either side), lambda=0.001 was already at the TV regularization optimum (both lambda-UP@0.003 and lambda-DOWN@0.0005 regress), confirming ~0.21 hr is the STRUCTURAL classical-TV ceiling on real Mayo LDCT and this lever is EXHAUSTED. BUDGET: zero-marginal-compute knob at the budget-proven tv_iterations=120 -> ~928s wall (77% of 1200s, ~272s margin; +10% variance ~1018s still under). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged. sbatch --time=00:30:00 SLURM safety net.

rationale: itnet_v3-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=0.0001, epochs=9, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=460, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=820, seed=42, rationale=iter-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). BASE_ITER=5 (the BEST: c16/ep9/train_n=400, hr 0.328842). ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 460 (MIDDLE coverage) at FIXED epochs=9 -- i.e. raise data coverage while HOLDING per-slice exposure at the proven 9x level. This is the clean single-knob test iter-6 could NOT run: iter-6 funded FULL data (tn579) by CUTTING epochs to 6 (parity), so it lost on BOTH axes vs iter-5 (grad_steps 3474<3600 AND exposure 6x<9x) and REGRESSED to hr 0.315239. iter-7 instead adds coverage at constant exposure. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) itnet_v3 trajectory: iter-1 ep8/tn200 hr 0.268409 (737.85s); iter-2 ep14/tn200 hr 0.310054 (1010.07s); iter-3 ep18/tn200 hr 0.312282 (1072.94s, epochs PLATEAUED); iter-4 ep9/c24/tn200 hr 0.295576 (834.0s, capacity REGRESSED -> revert c16); iter-5 BEST ep9/c16/tn400 hr 0.328842 / SSIM 0.915763 / PSNR 37.54 / RMSE 0.000664 (1006.81s=16.78min, 193s budget UNSPENT); iter-6 ep6/c16/tn579 hr 0.315239 / SSIM 0.906478 (914.0s=15.2min, 286s budget UNSPENT). PER-EPOCH COST scales LINEARLY with train_n (bs=1, 0.1723 s/slice): tn400->68.9s/ep, tn460->79.3s/ep, tn579->99.7s/ep. So at the 1200s wall full data (tn579) can only buy ep6-7 (<=7x exposure) while tn400 buys ep9-10 (9-10x). (2) LIMITER: the EPOCHS-vs-DATA tradeoff at the budget. iter-6 proved FULL data UNDER-TRAINS in-budget: tn579 only affords ep6 = 6x exposure, worse than tn400/ep9 = 9x. The per-epoch cost of the last 30% of data is too high to keep exposure at 9x. itnet_v3 needs ~9x exposure to converge in-budget (epochs plateaued only at ep18 on tn200; ep6 is clearly under-trained). So coverage is only worth raising IF exposure stays >=9x. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 400 -> 460, epochs HELD at 9 (NOT cut). This is the LARGEST train_n that still affords ep9 inside the wall: 481 fixed + 9*460*0.1723 = 1194s = 19.9 min < 1200s (and the model OVER-predicts by 95-165s -- iter-6 landed 165s under -- so real elapsed ~1060s/17.7min). It beats iter-5 on coverage (69%->79%) AND grad_steps (3600->4140) at IDENTICAL 9x exposure; it beats iter-6 on exposure (6x->9x) and grad_steps (3474->4140). tn480+ would force ep8 (8x exposure, below the proven 9x) so 460 is the sweet spot: max coverage at >=9x exposure. (4) HYPOTHESIS: adding 60 distinct training slices (400->460, 69%->79% coverage) WHILE HOLDING exposure at 9x lifts hr above the iter-5 best 0.328842, because iter-6 showed the data lever works ONLY when exposure is not sacrificed -- and here it is not. NUMERIC FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.3288 at tn460/ep9, itnet_v3 is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.329, the tn400/ep9 point) -- it cannot afford enough epochs on more data, and even coverage-at-constant-exposure does not help -> file the ceiling, stays #3. (5) BUDGET (HARD 1200s = train+score): fixed 481s, per_slice 0.1723s; epochs=(1200-481)/(460*0.1723)=9.07 -> ep9 is the max integer that fits. total=481+9*460*0.1723=1194s conservative (real ~1060s). Train-only=9*460*0.1723=713s < max_train_s=820 backstop, so it never truncates (checks between epochs; fences only runaway slowdown); the 214-slice per-sample val + figure always land inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-sample itnet.projector swap for the k=3 DC steps, bg_target=truth. (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign. Predicted iter-7 hr: 0.33-0.34 if coverage-at-9x-exposure helps; <=0.3288 falsifies -> budget-constrained ceiling at ~0.329, stays #3.

rationale: learned_primal_dual-claude-agentic: lpd_iters=5, lpd_hidden=48, lpd_n_primal=5, lpd_n_dual=5, lpd_share_weights=False, lr=0.0007, lr_schedule=cosine, epochs=6, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=iter-6 search-20260619-01: ONE knob = lpd_iters 3 -> 5 (UNROLL DEPTH), the LPD-DEFINING lever and the only remaining axis that directly tests the structural hypothesis. BASE_ITER=4 (best-SSIM config: lr=7e-4 cosine, lpd_hidden=48, n_primal=5, n_dual=5, batch=1, val_chunk=1, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). PRIOR ARC (ALL hr=0): SSIM 0.84271(it1 iters5/ep6/lr5e-4) -> 0.863635(it2) -> 0.885115(it3) -> 0.898033(it4 BEST, iters3/ep10/lr7e-4) -> 0.88446(it5 train_n300/ep7, epochs-cut-confounded but LOWEST RMSE 1.139e-3 yet STILL hr0). hr pinned at the LD-FBP floor the ENTIRE arc. LIMITER (STRUCTURAL CEILING, named): LPD is a projector-in-loop unrolled primal-dual net; its learned proximal updates only add value where the FBP adjoint leaves RESIDUAL STRUCTURE to recover (sparse/limited-view, ill-posed inverse). On DENSE 2304-view Mayo the LD-FBP is NEAR-COMPLETE (2304 views >> Nyquist; well-conditioned operator), so there is NO ill-posedness headroom for the unrolled updates to exploit -> LPD sharpens structure (rising SSIM) but cannot push RMSE below the already-near-optimal LD-FBP -> hr=0 regardless of capacity/epochs/lr/data. SAME mechanism makes LPD the breast/demo CHAMPION (128-view SPARSE -> FBP incomplete -> huge headroom) yet hr=0 on dense Mayo. iter-5 already FALSIFIED the data lever (train_n 200->300 fell to 0.88446). REMAINING UNTRIED AXIS = unroll DEPTH itself: lpd_iters 3->5 doubles-ish the learned primal-dual correction steps. If Mayo had ANY FBP-incompleteness headroom, deeper unrolling (the thing that makes LPD an unrolled net, not a U-Net) is exactly where it would surface. BUDGET MATH vs 1200s: iters=5 raises per-sample projector fwd+adj cost ~5/3x vs iters=3, so epochs traded 10->6 AND train_n 300->200 to hold the wall. EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED FIT: iter-1 ran iters5/ep6/tn200 = 1149.5s = 19.2min < 1200s; iter-6 is compute-identical (only lr 5e-4->7e-4 changes, lr does not change FLOPs) -> ~1150s, +50s margin. ep7 at iters5 would be ~1340s (OVER the wall) so ep6 is the budget-fit point; lpd_hidden^ stays OFF. HYP: deeper unroll at the TUNED lr 7e-4 (iter-1 was iters5 but at UNTUNED lr 5e-4 / first-feasibility ep6, scored 0.84271) extracts more FBP-residual correction; predict SSIM ~0.86-0.90, and IF any Mayo FBP-incompleteness exists, hr lifts >0 for the first time on LPD Mayo. FALSIFIER: hr stays 0.000 (and SSIM <= 0.898 since ep6 under-trains vs iter-4 ep10) => deeper unrolling does NOT help => DEFINITIVE structural ceiling: dense 2304-view LD-FBP is near-complete, LPD has no ill-posedness to exploit, FBP-bounded regardless of unroll depth. The path now DOCUMENTS the ceiling toward iter-20.

KEY SIGNAL the iter-4 author under-weighted: T25->T28 MOVED SSIM +0.085 (0.394->0.478) and PSNR +2.6dB (14.3->16.9) MONOTONICALLY -> T is the ONLY live lever and the 25-28 step DDIM schedule is too COARSE for the constrained hard-DC trajectory to converge; eta+relax are exhausted (both regressed when moved off iter-1s working point). rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=True, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). PRIOR TRAJECTORY (SSIM/hr): iter-1 K=10 0.2855/0.0; iter-2 K=30 0.2855/0.0 (byte-identical: depth FALSIFIED); iter-3 step=1e-8 0.8137/0.0 (LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH: loss flat 6.4e-5, lambda PINNED, step crept 1.06e-8->1.76e-8 -> near-identity on fbp_init, recon PSNR 33.60 just BELOW baseline 34.08); iter-4 step=1e-5 0.6949/0.0 PSNR 21.83. BEST hr = 0.0 across all 4; best SSIM = iter-3 0.8137 (but that is pure FBP passthrough, not a trained recon). BASE_ITER=4 (the ONLY iter where training actually un-froze). LIMITER (from iter-4 SLURM log 765355, the decisive evidence): at step_init=1e-5 the 60 free scalars FINALLY trained for real -- loss DROPPED 5.2e-5->2.8e-5 (first real decrease in the campaign), lambda[k] DEPARTED init (0.001->0.00111..0.00239), step[k] adapted. BUT SSIM got WORSE (0.8137->0.6949) and PSNR collapsed to 21.83. Root cause: with tv_share_steps=False the 30 INDEPENDENT per-iter log_step scalars are free to RUNAWAY -- step[1] exploded 6.3e-5->0.031 (epoch5-8), driving that single unrolled iterate back into the SATURATED-CLAMP regime that iter-1/2 proved kills the recon. The supervised-L2 loss decreased while SSIM/PSNR worsened = a degenerate per-step-instability basin (one runaway step the masked-L2 tolerates but the recon does not). The limiter is NO LONGER step scale (1e-5 IS the active training basin) NOR depth NOR epochs/lr -- it is the UNCONSTRAINED PER-STEP DEGREE OF FREEDOM letting individual steps diverge into the clamp. ONE KNOB CHANGED (from BASE_ITER=4): tv_share_steps False -> True (60 free scalars -> 2 shared scalars: ONE step + ONE lambda applied uniformly across all K=30 unrolled iterations). All else IDENTICAL to iter-4 (tv_step_init=1e-5 KEPT -- it is the confirmed active basin; tv_K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, lr=5e-2, tv_lambda_init=1e-3, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: a SHARED step/lambda cannot have a single runaway iterate -- it forces a uniform, stable K=30 GD that stays inside the [0,0.05] clamp basin while still TRAINING (the iter-4 log proved the scalars receive real gradient at step=1e-5). I expect SSIM to RECOVER above the 0.6949 iter-4 collapse and the trained-stable TV to finally exceed its own LD-FBP passthrough (SSIM > 0.8137, hr > 0) because the one trainable step now optimizes the data-vs-TV balance globally without any step being allowed to blow into clamp saturation. NUMERIC FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays <= 0.8137 with hr=0 (the shared step ALSO converges to either the passthrough floor (step->0) or the clamp ceiling (step->over-large), i.e. there is NO single shared step value in [0,0.05]-clamp-basin that both trains AND beats FBP), then the supervised-unrolled-TV harness is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on real Mayo 2304-view LDCT under the config-only contract (the shared solvers raw unnormalized-adjoint back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT and STOP iterating this solver at iter-5. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score=1200s): IDENTICAL compute to iter-4 (tv_share_steps changes ONLY the scalar COUNT 60->2, not any loop size: same K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, val_n=214, val_chunk=5) -> ~918s measured iter-4, ~282s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. PREDICTED iter-5: SSIM ~0.81-0.86, hr most-likely 0.0 (predicted ceiling MECHANISM if hr stays 0: the supervised-L2 + unnormalized 2304-view adjoint step has no shared scalar that both escapes the FBP-passthrough basin AND stays out of clamp saturation -- the trained-stable TV recovers toward the FBP floor but cannot strictly EXCEED its own LD-FBP because the only image-domain prior is a single global TV weight, structurally weaker than the LDCT noise it must remove). If hr>0, supervised-TV is repaired and iter-6 raises train_n (capacity is tiny -- 2 scalars -- so data lever is weak, weigh carefully).

rationale: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=3, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.04, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-5 (search-20260619-01, naf). SIX-BOX. (1) NUMBERS trajectory (monotone climb via leanness+lr, all hr=0): iter-1 hidden=128,layers=4,lr=1e-2 -> SSIM 0.4729 (PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08, elapsed 1097s, median ~91 Adam steps/scene at the 5.0s per-scene wall, 18-min outer wall 1080s hit EXACTLY at scene 214). iter-2 hidden 128->64 -> SSIM 0.4943 (+0.0215, PSNR 18.62). iter-3 layers 4->3 -> SSIM 0.5452 (+0.0509, PSNR 19.238, RMSE 0.005459). iter-4 lr 1e-2->2e-2 -> SSIM 0.5629 (+0.0177, PSNR 20.276, RMSE 0.004843, elapsed 1095.5s, params 0.006465M) = BEST. Still FAR below the LD-FBP cal floor (~0.81). (2) FAILURE MODE / LIMITER: budget-starved per-scene INR fit. The per-scene 5.0s t_limit (solver fit_one_scene break) governs, naf_n_iter=3000 is just a high cap; only ~90-100 Adam steps/scene leave the NeRF-style coordinate-MLP barely off its init_mu=0.005 water-mu init (a NeRF wants hundreds-to-thousands). Total budget 214x5.0s=1070s~=1080s outer wall is FULL inside the 20-min compute budget and CANNOT be raised. (3) ONE KNOB: naf_lr 2e-2->4e-2 (naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=3, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). The two LEANNESS levers are spent: hidden hit 64 (iter-2), layers hit 3 (iter-3) -- layers 3->2 zeros the range(layers-2) hidden loop -> single Linear(in,64)->Linear(64,1) perceptron capacity-cliff; n_freqs->6 trades positional-encoding bandwidth. lr is the ORTHOGONAL lever attacking the diagnosed too-few-steps-off-init failure WITHOUT shrinking the fixed model: in the ~90-100-step init-anchored Adam regime a higher lr travels further off init per step. iter-4 already PROVED this axis (1e-2->2e-2 gave +0.0177, PSNR up, RMSE down, NO instability), so continue it with another measured 2x step. Model held fixed so the SSIM delta isolates lr cleanly. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if naf_lr 2e-2->4e-2, SSIM rises above 0.5629 because each of the ~90-100 per-scene steps moves the INR further off its water-mu init within the same per-scene wall (same mechanism that gave iter-4 +0.0177). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stalls at ~0.56 or DROPS (lr-induced instability in the short Adam fit), the lr lever is exhausted -> NAF has hit the practical per-scene-INR ceiling in a 5s/214-scene budget (~0.56 vs LD-FBP ~0.81), a STRUCTURAL NEGATIVE on dense 2304-view Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT) to document toward iter-20. (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min, in-solver outer wall = governor) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap so the WALL governs). 214x5.0s=1070s~=1080s outer wall (hit exactly at scene 214 every iter; measured elapsed 1094.6-1100s, well inside the 30-min sbatch kill). lr change is cost-free. val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_2017 iter-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: batch_size 2 -> 1. BASE_ITER=5 (the BEST + only above-baseline point: SSIM 0.8114, hr 0.0319, ep19/bs2/lr5e-4/lambda0.0023/n_filters16) -- reverting AWAY from iter-6 (lr 3e-4 REGRESSED to 0.7883/hr0). epochs traded 19->10 purely to fit the HARD 1200s budget at bs=1 (NOT a second hypothesis knob); max_train_s 1100->1050 backstop. TRAJECTORY (corrected metric): iter-1 OOM(bs4); iter-2 0.8012 hr0; iter-3 0.7932 hr0 (lambda 0.0023->0.05 REGRESSED); iter-4 0.7828 hr0 (n_filters 16->4 REGRESSED); iter-5 0.8114 hr0.0319 KEEP (epochs 14->19, FIRST above the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, under-training diagnosis CONFIRMED); iter-6 0.7883 hr0 DISCARD (lr 5e-4->3e-4 REGRESSED -- lower lr starved the under-trained net, iter-6 falsifier TRIGGERED). best hr = 0.0319 @iter-5. LIMITER (box2): under-convergence at the wall-pinned epoch budget. iter-5 confirmed the epochs lever works but ep19 is WALL-PINNED (one more epoch overruns 1200s at 56.4s/epoch bs=2); iter-6 proved lr-down does not help (it starves, not stabilizes). The ONLY remaining within-budget step-count lever is batch_size DOWN: bs=1 doubles batches/epoch (train_n=200 -> 200 batches/epoch vs 100 at bs=2), i.e. doubles optimizer steps per epoch -- the iter-6 PRE-REGISTERED falsifier path (iter-6: if hr<=0.0319, iter-7 must trade gradient STEPS via batch_size 2->1). ONE KNOB CHOICE (box3): batch_size 2->1, base = iter-5 BEST (lr=5e-4 RESTORED, lambda=0.0023, n_filters=16, vn_T=5, kernel=11, n_bumps=31, x_range=2.0, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42 all held). HYPOTHESIS (box4): bs=1 gives 2x optimizer steps/epoch; even with epochs traded 19->10 the step count rises 1900 (bs2 x ep19) -> 2000 (bs1 x ep10 x 200/epoch), and each step on a smaller batch is a noisier/finer descent that the under-trained VN benefits from -> predict val_ssim rises above 0.8114 (hr > 0.0319), targeting ~0.82-0.83 / hr ~0.04-0.06. FALSIFIER (terminal): if hr <= 0.0319 at bs=1, hammernik_2017s 20-min budget is genuinely convergence-bounded -- doubling steps via bs-down cannot reach the proven ep38/bs1 (7600-step) convergence basin within 1200s -> its ceiling is ~0.032 and the budget-bounded ceiling is DOCUMENTED (no within-budget step-count lever remains: epochs wall-pinned, lr-down failed, bs already at the minimum). BUDGET (box5, HARD 1200s train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): bs=1 doubles batches/epoch AND loses within-batch parallelism + adds per-sample projector swaps, so per-epoch wall rises from 56.4s (bs2) to ~95-105s (bs1, ~1.7-1.9x). At ~105s/epoch x 10 epochs = ~1050s train + ~95s score(214)+figure = ~1145s predicted elapsed < 1200s; max_train_s=1050 backstop trips before the figure, well under the 1800s SLURM kill. If per-epoch lands lighter (~95s) the max_train_s wall stops training at ~ep11, still in-budget. MEMORY-SAFE (SAFER than bs=2): batch_size=1 HALVES the (B,F,H,W)=(1,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF activation tensors held across 5 unrolled steps vs bs=2 -- strictly less than the iter-5 footprint that already fit 16 GB (bs=4 was the OOM, bs=1 is the safest point). N_k=16, grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability).

(2) LIMITER = pretrain-then-FIXED-DC ceiling (structural, CONFIRMED from solver_itnet.py): main() lines 207-216 run itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() = pure INFERENCE; finetune_itnet() (line 114) is DEFINED but NEVER called; the k=3 DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable params (self.alpha is a plain float line 73, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN line 74). The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M 0.2329) pretrained FBP->truth (lines 197-200) that NEVER sees the DC steps. v1 is the STRUCTURAL TWIN of itnet_v2 (same pretrain-then-fixed-DC); the doc records v2 just tested train_n 200->400 and its denoiser SSIM climbed (0.7039->0.7294) but the untrained-DC capped hr at 0. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 300 (+50% data coverage; the FIXED-stratified subset via load_val_split n=train_n + randperm only ever sees 35% of the 579-slice pool at n=200). pretrain_epochs 220 -> 140 is NOT a second hypothesis-knob, it is the budget backstop to hold the HARD 20-min wall at near GRAD-STEP PARITY (200x220=44000 vs 300x140=42000, only -4.5% optimization) so the change isolates DATA COVERAGE, per the campaign train_n-lever protocol. FALSIFIER (operative): if hr > 0 at train_n=300 (v1 clears the ~0.81 FBP floor), v1 is DATA-LIMITED not structurally capped, and train_n is the live lever toward 20; implausible given v2 twin but the clean discriminator. PREDICTED iter-5 hr = 0.000 (SSIM ~0.71-0.72). rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=6, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=480, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB (DATA-COVERAGE lever): train_n 200 -> 480 (~35% -> ~83% of the 579-slice train pool). BASE = iter-1 BEST config (vn_n_filters=16, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_normalize_filters=False; NOT the regressed iter-2/3/4). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, ALL BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor, baseline_PSNR 34.08): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 PSNR 32.40 RMSE 1.199e-3 (N_k=16, lam=0.0023, elapsed 1295.7s) <- BEST; iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (N_k 16->24 capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 PSNR 32.07 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05 DC UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, 1159.6s); iter-4 SSIM 0.73363 PSNR 23.80 RMSE 3.228e-3 (vn_normalize_filters F->T -> REGRESSED -0.0346, 1339.8s). LIMITER / FAILURE MODE: every STRUCTURAL knob tried (capacity^, DC-weight^, filter-constraint) made it WORSE; loss flat by ep3 so it is NOT under-training; the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) collapses to a BLUNT SMOOTHER that drags the recon monotonically below its own FBP init. iter-4's terminal falsifier ('SSIM<=0.84 with the regulariser constrained -> structurally FBP-bounded') FIRED. BUT one axis is UNTESTED and shared by ALL 4 iters: every iter trained on the SAME 200/579 (35%) stratified subset. MECHANISM CONFIRMED (this turn): hammernik_vn build_dataset calls load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) = a FIXED stratified subset chosen ONCE (round-robin across ps-groups, sel=sorted(picks)), then the train loop reshuffles ONLY that subset via torch.randperm(train_n) per epoch -- it does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset. So train_n=200 = the net only ever sees 35% of the 579-slice train pool -> train_n IS a LIVE data-coverage lever (same mechanism as uswin train_n 200->480 hr 0.3532->0.3829 and itnet_v3 200->400 hr 0.3123->0.3288). This is the strongest untried axis AND the cleanest single-knob test of whether the regulariser degradation is data-coverage-starved (200 slices too few for the 16-filter bank to learn an edge-preserving rather than smoothing regulariser) vs a true structural ceiling. HYPOTHESIS: if the degradation is data-starved, train_n 200->480 lifts val_ssim above the iter-1 0.80528 and toward/over the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER (terminal): if val_ssim stays <=0.81 (still <FBP, hr=0) even at 2.4x the training data, hammernik_vn is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on rebinned 2304-view Mayo LDCT with the data-coverage lever EXHAUSTED -> file the negative result and drive remaining iters to document the ceiling. GRAD-STEP PARITY (isolate DATA COVERAGE from extra optimization): iter-1 was max_train_s=1000-bound and ran ~7 epochs at 200 slices = ~1400 grad-slices. At train_n=480, max_train_s=1000 (kept) caps ~2.9 epochs (480x2.9 ~= 1392 grad-slices) -> near-identical optimization budget, so the comparison isolates COVERAGE not extra steps. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): iter-1 trained ~7 ep / 1000s at 200 slices => ~143 s/ep => ~0.715 s/slice/ep; at 480 slices ~343 s/ep, so max_train_s=1000 trips at ~2.9 ep (epochs=6 is just an upper bound the wall trips first). Total ~= 1000 (train wall) + ~160 (score 214 + figure) ~= 1160s, under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical per-step footprint to iter-1 (batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=16 within the 16 GB RTX5000; cf. hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).

rationale: dual_domain_supervised-claude-agentic: unet_c=16, lr=0.0001, epochs=9, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=579, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). START FROM iter-3 BEST (c16/ep27/lr1e-4), NOT iter-4's regressed c24. ONE KNOB (training-data coverage): train_n 200 -> 579 (the FULL Wagner train pool), with epochs TRADED DOWN 27 -> 9 as the forced budget-coupling to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) iter-3 best: SSIM 0.918191 / hr 0.365357 at unet_c=16/epochs=27/lr=1e-4/train_n=200, elapsed_s=1151.40s (19.2 min, near the wall). (2) LIMITER: epochs AND capacity are both EXHAUSTED. The epochs lever was monotone (ep8 hr0.276 -> ep20 0.339 -> ep27 0.3654) but is WALL-LOCKED (iter-3 ep27 used 1151.4/1200s; ep32 -> 1366s busts). The capacity lever REGRESSED (iter-4 c24/ep10 -> hr 0.298560, BELOW iter-3, because trading 27->10 epochs to fund 2.25x conv-compute under-trained the bigger net). No lr-schedule is wired (FORBIDDEN to edit the shared solver). Is the champion DATA-COVERAGE-limited? iter-3 trained on only train_n=200 of the 579-slice train pool (CONFIRMED: solver_dual_ddomain_supervised.py build_dataset -> load_val_split(kind='mayo_ldct_2d', split='train', n=train_n) slices n_eff=min(train_n,n_truth) DISTINCT stratified slices ONCE and trains the SAME fixed set every epoch via torch.randperm reshuffle -- NO RotatingSubsetDataset rotation in this path, so train_n is a GENUINE live lever, NOT inert; 379 of the 579 train slices were UNUSED at train_n=200). The val FIGURE's harness metadata field train_n=400 is a cosmetic TRAIN_N-env default in claude_agentic_one_iter.py:185/263 and does NOT override the solver's cfg train_n -- the solver uses cfg['train_n'] from this JSON. (3) ONE KNOB: training data train_n 200->579 (use the ENTIRE Wagner train set; stratified round-robin spans all 3 ps-groups 0.66192:154 + 0.73979:98 + 0.77873:327 = 579). At train_n=579: per_epoch=579*0.1977=114.5s and fixed ~125s (val=214 is train_n-independent; +~23s extra data-load for 379 more slices). epochs=9 predicts 125 + 9*114.5 = 1155s = 19.3 min (~45s margin inside the 1200s budget; sbatch wall 30 min). epochs=10 -> 1270s = 21.2 min BUSTS the 20-min wall, so 10 is NOT chosen; 9 is the largest epoch count the full-pool timing permits. (Model calibration: it predicts iter-3 ep27 at 1170s vs actual 1151.4s, within 1.6%.) (4) HYPOTHESIS: 2.9x more distinct training slices (200->579, the full pool) lifts hr ABOVE the iter-3 champion 0.365357 even at the reduced ep9, because at train_n=200 the supervised DD-UNet sees only ~35% of the Wagner train anatomy and is data-coverage-limited on the held-out L277 val patient (better train-set diversity -> better generalisation under the 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). FALSIFIER (in NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.365357 at train_n=579/ep9, the DD-UNet is at its BUDGET-CONSTRAINED CEILING on this val set (~0.37) and ALL THREE levers -- epochs (wall-locked), capacity (regressed iter-4), AND data coverage (this iter) -- are EXHAUSTED -> file the CHAMPION-CEILING verdict for dual_domain_supervised. (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val=ALL 214 L277 slices; grad_clip=1.0 (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients ~18x -> lr kept conservative at 1e-4 + nonfinite-grad-skip). (6) no control return. rationale: learned_primal_dual-claude-agentic: lpd_iters=3, lpd_hidden=48, lpd_n_primal=5, lpd_n_dual=5, lpd_share_weights=False, lr=0.0007, lr_schedule=cosine, epochs=7, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=300, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 search-20260619-01: ONE knob = train_n 200 -> 300 (the ONLY untried lever on LPD's Mayo arc). Everything physics/capacity held at iter-4's budget-compliant best-SSIM point (lpd_iters=3, hidden=48, n_primal=5, n_dual=5, lr=7e-4 cosine, batch=1, val_chunk=1, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); epochs traded 10 -> 7 PURELY to hold the HARD 20-min wall (see budget math). WHY DATA IS NOT INERT: the LPD solver loads a FIXED train_n subset ONCE via build_dataset->load_val_split (solver L81), then torch.randperm reshuffles that SAME fixed tensor each epoch (solver L257). There is NO per-epoch RotatingSubsetDataset rotation in this solver path, so train_n=200 has only ever shown the net 200 distinct slices out of the 579-slice train pool (3 patients: ps-groups 154/98/327). At Mayo train_n the loader stratifies round-robin across the 3 ps-groups, so 200->300 adds ~100 genuinely-new distinct slices spanning all 3 train patients (group-2 caps at 98) => +50% effective training set, still patient-balanced. LIMITER REFRAME: the SSIM 0.843->0.864->0.885->0.898 arc was driven by epochs (under-training), then lr (iter-4), with hr pinned at the LD-FBP floor (0.000) the WHOLE way; epochs is now wall-capped and lr is spent, but the net has NEVER seen more than 200/579 slices. Data-coverage is the unexamined axis. BUDGET MATH vs 1200s/20-min wall: total job time scales with total gradient steps = epochs*train_n (batch=1) + a small fixed ~95s (cuda init + the fixed 214-slice val pass). iter-4 = 2000 steps (ep10*tn200) ran 1100.7s=18.35min => conservative 0.503 s/step. iter-5 = 2100 steps (ep7*tn300) -> model 1151s=19.18min, +49s margin under the 1200s wall (ep8*tn300=2400 steps=21.7min OVERshoots; ep7 is the budget-fit epoch count for tn300). lpd_hidden^/lpd_iters^ stay OFF (add per-sample projector fwd+adj cost, blow the wall). HYP: +50% distinct (still patient-balanced) training data lets the LPD generalise to the held-out val patient L277 better than 200 slices did, lifting SSIM (predict ~0.90-0.92) and, if the extra coverage adds real high-frequency structure the 200-slice net was missing, pushing RMSE down enough to clear the LD-FBP floor (hr>0) for the first time on LPD's Mayo arc. FALSIFIER: SSIM plateaus at/below 0.898 (iter-4) AND hr still 0.000 => more data is NOT the lever; LPD is at its budget-constrained ceiling on 2304-view Mayo (~0.90 SSIM, hr 0) -- a projector-in-loop unrolled net that sharpens structure (rising SSIM) but cannot beat FBP on PSNR/RMSE within the 20-min budget at this capacity. The epochs-down-to-7 confound is bounded: if SSIM DROPS below iter-2's 0.864 (ep10/tn200) the cut went too far and tn300 needs a deeper wall, not this budget.

LIMITER REFRAME: the SSIM 0.843->0.864->0.885->0.898 arc was driven by epochs (under-training), then lr (iter-4), with hr pinned at the LD-FBP floor (0.000) the WHOLE way; epochs is now wall-capped and lr is spent, but the net has NEVER seen more than 200/579 slices. Data-coverage is the unexamined axis. BUDGET MATH vs 1200s/20-min wall: total job time scales with total gradient steps = epochs*train_n (batch=1) + a small fixed ~95s (cuda init + the fixed 214-slice val pass). iter-4 = 2000 steps (ep10*tn200) ran 1100.7s=18.35min => conservative 0.503 s/step. iter-5 = 2100 steps (ep7*tn300) -> model 1151s=19.18min, +49s margin under the 1200s wall (ep8*tn300=2400 steps=21.7min OVERshoots; ep7 is the budget-fit epoch count for tn300). lpd_hidden^/lpd_iters^ stay OFF (add per-sample projector fwd+adj cost, blow the wall). ONE KNOB: TRAINING DATA train_n 200 -> 480 (2.4x), with epochs TRADED DOWN 64 -> 26 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. uswin_c reverts 32 -> 24 (iter-3 best), all else identical to iter-3 (val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (1) iter-3 BEST: SSIM 0.924443 / hr 0.353196 / PSNR 37.86 in elapsed_s=1085.87, train_n=200, c24, ep64 (#2 on the Mayo board). iter-4 (c32/ep34) REGRESSED to hr 0.272533 (SSIM 0.892773) in 760.76s -> the capacity-for-epochs trade FAILED: ep34 under-trained the 6.9M-param c32 net more than the added capacity helped (iter-4's own falsifier (b): revert to c24 and treat 0.3532 as ceiling UNLESS an untried lever exists). (2) LIMITER: epochs are WALL-LOCKED (iter-3 ep64 used 1085.87s = 90.5pct of 1200s; ep72 would bust) AND show diminishing returns (+0.149 hr over ep10->40 but only +0.031 over ep40->64); capacity REGRESSED (iter-4). At train_n=480 per_epoch = 480*0.07255 = 34.82 s/epoch. WORST CASE (+10pct/sample variance, +5pct fixed): ep26 worst elapsed = 165.2 + 26*480*0.07981 = 1161s = 19.4 min (39s margin inside 1200s); ep28 worst = 1238s BUSTS -> ep26 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit even the worst case. REALISTIC: ep26 = 157.3 + 26*34.82 = 1063s = 17.7 min (comfortable). Train-only worst = 26*480*0.07981 = 996s; max_train_s=980 set as the HARD train-only backstop so even at hot per-sample cost train halts <=980s leaving >=220s for the worst-case 214-slice val+figure inside the 1200s budget. (4) HYPOTHESIS: more training data (200->480 distinct slices spanning all 3 train patients) lifts hr above the iter-3 0.353196, because uswin's hr flattened with epochs (training-basin at 200 samples) AND regressed with capacity (iter-4) -- the remaining slack is GENERALISATION to the unseen val patient, which broader patient coverage addresses. Predicted iter-5 hr ~0.37-0.40. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.353196 at train_n=480/ep26, uswin is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.35) on this val set and ALL three levers (epochs, capacity, data) are exhausted -> iter-6 reverts to the iter-3 c24/ep64/train_n=200 config and accepts 0.3532 as the uswin Mayo ceiling. (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices (NOT reduced); grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). (6) no control return.

rationale: itnet_v3-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=0.0001, epochs=9, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=400, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=720, seed=42, rationale=iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). START FROM iter-3 BEST (c16/ep18, hr 0.3123), NOT iter-4's regressed c24. ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 400 (TRAINING DATA = the one untried lever), with epochs traded DOWN 18 -> 9 to (a) hold total gradient steps at PARITY with iter-3 best (400*9 = 3600 = 200*18) so any hr change isolates DATA COVERAGE, not extra optimization, and (b) fit the HARD 20-min train+score wall. All else = iter-3 best exactly (itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, lr=1e-4, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-3 BEST = SSIM 0.904773 / hr 0.312282 / PSNR 37.33 / RMSE 0.000680 at c16/ep18/train_n=200, elapsed 1072.94s = 17.88 min, params 3.699M. iter-4 (c24/ep9, capacity-up) REGRESSED to SSIM 0.899304 / hr 0.295576 -> capacity is NOT the lever; revert to c16. (2) LIMITER: epochs PLATEAUED (iter-2 ep14 hr 0.3101 -> iter-3 ep18 hr 0.3123, +0.0022, SSIM even dropped) AND capacity-for-epochs REGRESSED (iter-4). The remaining limiter is DATA COVERAGE: the itnet_v3 solver loads a FIXED stratified train subset ONCE via build_dataset -> load_val_split(split='train', n=train_n) (solver_itnet_v3.py lines 198-199) and merely RESHUFFLES that same subset every epoch (torch.randperm(train_n), line 235). It does NOT use RotatingSubsetDataset, so train_n=200 means the net has only ever seen 200 of the 579 available train slices -> data-coverage-limited. train_n IS load-bearing here (NOT inert): the full pool is 579 slices across 3 ps-groups/patients (154 @0.66192, 98 @0.73979, 327 @0.77873); train_n=200 used only 35pct of it. (3) ONE KNOB: train_n 200 -> 400 (2x distinct slices = 69pct of the 579-slice pool; the stratified round-robin spans all 3 train patients more densely). epochs traded 18 -> 9 to fund it at grad-step parity (3600). (4) HYPOTHESIS: doubling distinct training slices (200 -> 400) lifts hr above the 0.3123 iter-3 best, because itnet_v3 is data-coverage-limited (epochs + capacity both exhausted) and a denser, more representative train set generalises better to the held-out L277 val patient. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.3123 at train_n=400 (all else iter-3-best, grad steps held at 3600), itnet_v3 is at its budget-constrained ceiling (~0.31) on this 214-slice / 321px-FOV Mayo val set with ALL three levers (epochs, capacity, data) exhausted -> iter-6 would have to change the metric basis or accept the ceiling. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): from the three c16/train_n=200 points (8,737.85),(14,1010.07),(18,1072.94) a least-squares fit gives per-epoch 34.45 s/epoch (covering 200 samples) + fixed 481.0 s (data load + per-sample-ps projector cache + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup). Per-epoch scales LINEARLY with train_n (bs=1 -> train_n steps/epoch), so train_n=400 -> per-epoch 68.9 s. At epochs=9: 481.0 + 9*68.9 = 1101 s = 18.35 min < 1200 s with ~99 s headroom. epochs=10 -> 1170 s = 19.5 min (tight); epochs=9 is the safe largest count at train_n=400 that also holds grad-step parity. Train alone at 9 ep = 9*68.9 = 620 s < max_train_s=720 backstop, so the backstop does not truncate (checks between epochs; only fences runaway slowdown) and a finite recon + 214-slice val + figure always land inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside dc_step overflows otherwise). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-sample itnet.projector swap for the k=3 DC steps, bg_target=truth. (6) do NOT return control mid-campaign. Predicted iter-5 hr: >0.3123 (target 0.32-0.34) if data-coverage-limited hypothesis holds; <=0.3123 falsifies -> budget-constrained ceiling, all levers exhausted.

rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_unconstrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=2, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-4 search-20260619-01 CONFIRMATION iter UNCONSTRAINED diff-recon vs reused Mayo DDPM v4 ckpt (ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt). ONE KNOB: recon_dcstep_every 0 -> 5 (turn ON the hard-CG data-consistency projection inside the otherwise-soft DPS reverse path -- the LAST UNTRIED lever). recon_dcstep_n_cg 3 -> 2 and recon_sample_steps 32 -> 25 are BUDGET-FORCED, not free choices: enabling hard-DC adds n_cg*(2 fwd + 1 back) projector calls per triggered step, so I must shrink the base trajectory to keep the 20-min wall (see BUDGET below); n_steps=25 is exactly the iter-2 base where eta=5 was already well-behaved, so the soft sub-path is held at its settled point and the every:0->5 flip is the only mechanistic change. recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=false, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 (FULL hard projection), recon_dcstep_warmup=5 all UNCHANGED. TRAJECTORY (corrected 214-slice / 321px-FOV metric): iter-1 (n_steps=25, eta=30, every=0) SSIM 0.3688 hr=0 PSNR 10.55 868.65s; iter-2 (25, eta=5, every=0) SSIM 0.3960 hr=0 PSNR 11.25 868.33s -- BEST SO FAR; iter-3 (32, eta=5, every=0) SSIM 0.3869 hr=0 PSNR 11.08 1103.8s -- longer DDIM trajectory did NOT help (slightly DOWN). All three sit in the 0.37-0.40 band, FAR below the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 and even below the FBP init. The two soft levers -- DPS guidance gain (eta 30->5) and trajectory length (n_steps 25->32) -- are now EXHAUSTED and FLAT, and the constrained sibling (eta 30->1 + hard-CG every=5) REGRESSED 0.39->0.24, so neither soft guidance nor capacity is the issue. FAILURE MODE (the hypothesis under final test): the recon is dominated by a Mayo v4 DDPM PRIOR that is STRUCTURALLY MISMATCHED to the rebinned-Mayo distribution -- globally faithful (plausible CT texture) but NOT conditionally faithful to the input sino under DPS, exactly the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict (4x-16x capacity + 2.5x training all stayed in 0.3-0.5 SSIM). recon_dcstep_every is the LAST untried mechanism that could falsify this: a Resample-style FULL hard-CG projection (relax=1.0) onto the measurement manifold is a STRONGER fidelity backstop than the soft DPS gradient -- it directly minimizes ||A x_mu - y||^2 by n_cg Gauss-Newton steps every 5 reverse steps, re-noising back to t_next. If the prior were merely under-guided, hard-DC would pull the recon decisively toward the sino and clear (or approach) the FBP floor; if the prior is structurally mismatched, the re-noise step injects the mismatched prior right back and the recon stays in the 0.37-0.42 band regardless. BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s wall, val=ALL 214 L277 slices): calibrated linear cost from the two measured points (iter-2 25-step every=0 = 4.058 s/slice; iter-3 32-step every=0 = 5.158 s/slice) gives per-step a=0.1572 s/step/slice + fixed offset b=0.127 s/slice, so one projector call ~ a/3 = 0.0524 s/call/slice. At n_steps=25, warmup=5, every=5 the DC-step triggers at k=5,10,15,20 (4 triggers, t_next>0), each adding n_cg=2 * (2 fwd + 1 back) = 6 projector calls = 6*0.0524 = 0.314 s/slice/trigger -> +1.26 s/slice total. Per-slice = 4.06 + 1.26 = 5.32 s -> 214 * 5.32 = 1137 s = 19.0 min < 1200 s wall (~63 s headroom, MORE in practice since the fixed offset b does not scale with DC). n_cg=3 (1272s=21.2min) or n_steps=28 (1306s) or every=4 (1205s) all BLOW the wall, so n_steps=25 / every=5 / n_cg=2 is the LARGEST hard-DC dose that fits -- the right budget-feasible probe. SIX-BOX PREDICTION: SSIM <= 0.42, hr = 0 (the structural-prior-mismatch hypothesis). FALSIFIER: if SSIM CLEARS the 0.8078 LD-FBP floor (or moves decisively toward it, say >0.6), the Mayo v4 DDPM prior was NOT structurally mismatched -- it was fidelity-starved, and hard-DC is the fix; redirect future iters to tuning the hard-DC dose (relax/n_cg/every). If SSIM STAYS in the 0.37-0.42 band (FBP floor uncleared even with full hard-CG fidelity), FILE THE DIFFUSION-PRIOR-MISMATCH VERDICT: the lever is the prior CLASS, not any sampler/fidelity hyperparameter (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 decision), STOP iterating diffusion-recon on Mayo, and the BEST run stays iter-2 (SSIM 0.396, hr 0). val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default -- not passing fov=False).

rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.02, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-5 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the BEST config family (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001) at the BUDGET-PROVEN tv_iterations=120 (NOT iter-4's 160 -- see BUDGET below). ONE KNOB: tv_lr 0.01->0.02 (all else IDENTICAL to the iter-2 BEST: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=120, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) = the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) REGRESSED (lambda-up exhausted); iter-4 SSIM 0.926664 hr 0.208547 RMSE 7.825e-4 (tv_iterations 120->160, 1227.4s). KEY RECONCILIATION OF THE PLANNED 160->200 KNOB: iter-4's measured elapsed_s was 1227.4s -- already OVER the 1200s HARD 20-min budget at 160 iters -- and 160 iters lifted hr only +0.0031 over the 120-iter iter-2 (0.205364->0.208547), within noise. HYPOTHESIS: doubling the step size (tv_lr 0.01->0.02) lets each of the budget-safe 120 gradient-descent steps travel ~2x further down the data-term gradient, so the recon reaches a LOWER data-term residual within 120 steps (the same/lower residual the 160-iter run was crawling toward) at ZERO extra compute, lowering val_rmse below 7.825e-4 so hr rises above iter-4's 0.208547 -- the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual. Why lr is the right convergence lever and not more iters: the GD schedule is step = lr/(1+decay*it), so with decay=0.01 the per-step distance shrinks ~2.4x by it=119; raising base lr counteracts that decay and converges the data term in fewer steps -- the budget-free way to test the convergence-vs-ceiling question the iter-4 falsifier left open. BUDGET: tv_lr is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- tv_iterations stays at the budget-proven 120 -> identical ~928s wall (cost model: 31.8 + 120*7.47 = 928s, 77% of the 1200s budget, ~272s margin; even at +10% GPU-contention step-cost variance it lands ~1018s, still comfortably under the wall). This DELIBERATELY reverts the over-budget tv_iterations=160 back to 120: the 20-min budget is HARD with no exceptions (six-box rule 5), and iter-4 at 160 already breached it. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.

rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=100, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-4 TERMINAL CONFIRMATION (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 60->100 (the only unmapped interior point between iter-3's 60 and iter-1's 150). FAILURE MODE (now structurally established across 3 iters): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training, no amortization) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at the hard 20-min wall. The exact [fit] outer-wall scene counts from the SLURM logs: iter-1 n_iter=150 -> sample 26 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335; iter-2 n_iter=400 -> sample 10 (4.7%), SSIM 0.736981; iter-3 n_iter=60 -> sample 64 (30%), SSIM 0.680981. BOTH levers are now REFUTED in NUMBERS: (a) iter-2 QUALITY lever -- 2.67x more Adam steps (150->400) moved the 214-avg by -0.0001 (FLAT); (b) iter-3 COVERAGE lever -- 2.5x more completed scenes (26->64) DROPPED the 214-avg by -0.057 (0.7383->0.6810). The iter-3 drop is the decisive signal: a partially-converged 60-step Gaussian recon scores BELOW the LD-FBP init it replaces, so adding fit-scenes is net-DESTRUCTIVE -- per-scene Gaussian splatting needs far more than 60-150 Adam steps to even match FBP on dense 2304-view Mayo (the discarded 20260614 run needed ~6000 iters/scene to reach SSIM 0.89-0.92, which at 0.282 s/step is 28 min/scene -> 0 of 214 scenes fit in 20 min). The 214-avg is a mixture: completed scenes are scored at their (under-fit, sub-FBP) Gaussian recon, the rest at their ~0.808 FBP-init; the peak of the mixture sits where FEW scenes are touched and most keep their good FBP init -- i.e. near iter-1's n_iter=150 / 26 scenes (0.7383). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the (coverage, SSIM) curve is smooth and monotone over [60,150]; n_iter=100 -> per-scene 0.282*100 = 28.2 s -> 1080/28.2 = ~38/214 scenes -> predicted SSIM in (0.681, 0.738), strictly BELOW iter-1's 0.738. PREDICTION: SSIM <= 0.74, hr 0. FALSIFIER: if n_iter=100 BEATS 0.738335 (iter-1 best), an interior quality-vs-coverage optimum exists and 150 is NOT the peak -> re-map. If n_iter=100 lands in (0.681, 0.738) as predicted, NO gs_n_iter beats 0.7383 -> file the STRUCTURAL budget-incompatibility verdict: R2-Gaussian cannot simultaneously cover all 214 slices AND fit any scene above its FBP init within the 20-min wall; best stays iter-1 (n_iter=150, SSIM 0.7383, hr=0, BELOW the 0.808 LD-FBP baseline). BUDGET MATH: 38 scenes * 28.2 s = 1072s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/2/3); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-1 0.7383 (26/214, BEST) -> iter-4 predicted ~0.71-0.73 (38/214) -> iter-3 0.6810 (64/214). Monotone-decreasing in coverage -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol (documented NEGATIVE RESULT).

rationale: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.0001, pretrain_epochs=240, pretrain_patience=240, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=1150, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). CONFIRMATION iter. ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 144->240 (1.67x); pretrain_patience tracked 144->240 so early-stop never fires before the full run (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1/2/3 where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-3 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 1100->1150 (19.2-min HARD backstop) to admit the longer pretrain inside the 20-min train+score budget while leaving the figure outside. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) TRAJECTORY: iter-1 SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=12 in elapsed_s=170.2; iter-2 SSIM 0.5888 / hr 0.000 @ep48 in 345.2s; iter-3 SSIM 0.6230 / hr 0.000 @ep144 in 744.1s (val_psnr 24.51, val_rmse 0.002976). Epoch->SSIM gain is sharply DIMINISHING: 12->48 (4x) gave +0.133, 48->144 (3x) gave only +0.034. hr=0 throughout (LD-FBP floor ~0.81, far above; end-to-end v3 sibling reaches 0.91). (2) LIMITER (CONFIRMED, structural): the DC stage in solver_itnet_v2.py has NO trainable params -- pretrain_denoiser trains ONLY the SmallUNet on (fbp,truth) residual pairs, then ItNetV2 runs itnet.eval() with the k=3 DC operator FIXED (log_alpha never optimized). More pretraining only sharpens the denoiser; it cannot fix the un-trained DC coupling, so v2 caps far below end-to-end v3 (0.91). iter-3's +0.034 over 3x epochs is the asymptote signature. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 144->240 (1.67x) -- the largest epoch bump the 20-min budget admits, to CONFIRM the asymptote. Chosen over a DC-stage knob (itnet_k/itnet_alpha_init carry no trainable weight -- changing them shifts a fixed operator, near-zero diagnostic value) and over lr-up (v3 unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe sibling move). With a pretrain-then-FIXED-DC architecture, pretrain_epochs is the ONLY learnable lever; pushing it as far as the budget allows is the cleanest confirmation of the pretrain-fixed-DC ceiling. (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: if pretrain_epochs 144->240, val_ssim lands ~0.63 (asymptoting, NOT the ~0.91 v3 band) with hr still 0.000, then itnet_v2's pretrain-then-FIXED-DC scheme is STRUCTURALLY CAPPED on Mayo regardless of epochs -- the un-trained DC operator, not under-training, is the limiter -- and the campaign documents v2 as a budget/architecture ceiling and prefers end-to-end v3. The +0.034/3x-epochs diminishing return predicts SSIM ~0.63-0.66 and hr 0. CONVERSELY (falsifier) if hr finally CLEARS 0 (val_ssim jumps past the 0.81 FBP floor), the cap was pretrain-epochs after all and iter-5 keeps climbing. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. Per-epoch slope from iter-2->iter-3 = (744.1-345.2)/(144-48) = 4.155 s/epoch; fixed (214-slice per-sample val + figure) = 345.2 - 48*4.155 = 145.8s. 240 ep -> 240*4.155 + 145.8 = 1143s, UNDER the 1200s (20-min) train+score budget and well within the 30-min sbatch wall. max_train_s=1150 is the HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the wall (if pretrain hits the clamp it stops gracefully and val still runs). val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override). residual_learning=False KEPT (the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual and collapses eval to ~0.34).

rationale: itnet-claude-agentic: pretrain_epochs=220, pretrain_lr=0.0001, itnet_k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, finetune_epochs=0, finetune_lr=0.0001, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric) for itnet = ItNet v1 (pretrain-denoiser-then-FIXED-DC, solver_itnet.py). This is a CONFIRMATION iter -- the solver is well-characterized; the goal is to confirm the asymptote of the only trainable lever, not to find a breakthrough. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS, not CT pixels). (1) PRIOR RESULTS (val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV): iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.4413 / hr 0.000, elapsed 191.1s; iter-2 ep48 -> SSIM 0.5927 / hr 0.000, elapsed 387.4s; iter-3 ep160 -> SSIM 0.6430 / hr 0.000, PSNR 24.67, RMSE 0.002922, elapsed 858.9s, params_M 0.2329. The pretrain_epochs lever is in clear diminishing returns: SSIM deltas are +0.151 (8->48), then +0.050 (48->160); hr has stayed PINNED at 0.000 across ALL three iters -- v1 remains BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor (and far below the END-TO-END sibling itnet_v3's ~0.91 / hr ~0.31). v1 (0.44->0.59->0.64) and its lever-twin itnet_v2 (0.59->0.62) trace the SAME under-0.81 curve; v3 is on a different curve entirely. (2) LIMITER = the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC CEILING (structural, confirmed by reading solver_itnet.py): finetune_itnet() is DEFINED (lines 114-135) but NEVER called in main(); the k=3 ItNet DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable params (self.alpha is a plain float, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN); itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() (lines 208-209) run the unroll as pure INFERENCE. The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M=0.2329), pretrained as an FBP->truth denoiser that NEVER sees the DC steps. pretrain_epochs is the sole lever and the fixed untrained DC post-processor caps v1 far below v3. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 160 -> 220 (1.375x). All else identical to iter-3 (k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, pretrain_lr=1e-4, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: a final confirmation push of the only trainable component to nail the asymptote. HYPOTHESIS: SSIM lands ~0.65 (asymptoting -- the diminishing +0.151 -> +0.050 slope predicts roughly +0.01-class for 160->220), hr STAYS 0.000. FALSIFIER (the operative one): if hr is STILL 0.000 (SSIM ~0.65, well below the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor and far below v3's 0.91), the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC architecture is STRUCTURALLY capped -- NOT under-trained -- and the campaign should FILE THE STRUCTURAL VERDICT for itnet v1 (epochs lever exhausted; future Mayo recon goes to the end-to-end itnet_v3, ~0.91) rather than spend more iters on v1's epochs. The counter-hypothesis (v1 suddenly clears 0.81 at 220 ep) is implausible given the measured +0.151 -> +0.050 slope. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): from the two latest measured points the per-epoch pretrain cost is (858.9-387.4)/(160-48) = 4.21 s/epoch and the fixed cost (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup) is 858.9 - 160*4.21 = 185.3 s (this exactly reproduces iter-3: 185.3 + 160*4.21 = 858.9). pretrain_epochs=220 predicts 185.3 + 220*4.21 = 1111 s = 18.5 min, inside the 1200s budget with ~1.5 min margin; ep240 would predict 1196s (too tight), so 220 is the largest safe confirmation push. The sbatch wall is 30 min, so the 18.5-min prediction leaves ample fence headroom. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default; NO fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside the DC step overflows otherwise). v1 has NO max_train_s backstop, so the 30-min sbatch wall is the only hard fence. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each val slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override).

rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=4, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_2017 iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). TERMINAL regularizer-attack iter. NOTE: the prompt's nominal lever vn_normalize_filters does NOT exist in solver_hammernik_2017.py (verified: this solver is a PURE IMAGE-DOMAIN VN that consumes only vn_T/vn_n_filters/vn_kernel/vn_n_bumps/vn_x_range/vn_*_init_std/vn_lambda_init/epochs/batch_size/lr/grad_clip/train_n/val_n/seed/max_train_s; vn_normalize_filters belongs to the SIBLING projector-in-loop hammernik_vn solver, which is testing exactly that knob in parallel job 765379 iter-4). Per the prompt's explicit fallback and iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier, iter-4 attacks the REGULARIZER ITSELF via the leanest config that avoids the DC-smoothing collapse: ONE KNOB vn_n_filters 16 -> 4 (shrink the analysis-filter bank 4x). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=5e-4, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, corrected metric, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 OOM at batch_size=4 (no recon, elapsed 72s); iter-2 SSIM 0.80123 (FIRST valid datapoint, PSNR 33.91, RMSE 0.00101, baseline_PSNR 34.08, elapsed 887s); iter-3 SSIM 0.793173 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.008, PSNR 33.92, RMSE 0.001007, elapsed 895.8s). BOTH levers tried so far regressed: capacity-as-it-was AND DC-weight-up. FAILURE MODE (well-characterized, confirmed cross-sibling): the learned VN regularizer term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i y) (solver line 141) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init y_NN below baseline, and at iter-3 lambda_t stayed pinned at init across all 14 epochs (Adam never grew the DC weight), so the lambda-anchor cannot save it. The sibling hammernik_vn shows the SAME signature: iter-1 0.8053 -> iter-2 0.7920 (filters UP regressed) -> iter-3 0.7682 (lambda UP regressed), monotone below FBP. ONE KNOB CHOICE: vn_n_filters 16 -> 4 is the most-diagnostic remaining regularizer attack in THIS solver. Shrinking the analysis-filter bank 4x structurally minimizes the degrees of freedom of the smoothing term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i y) -- the leanest learned-regularizer that still leaves a learned term at all. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation is the over-parameterized 16-filter bank collapsing into a low-pass smoother of the FBP init, a 4-filter bank has far less capacity to over-smooth -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init. (x_range/kernel held; n_filters is the single cleanest capacity-of-the-regularizer knob.) HYPOTHESIS: with the filter bank shrunk 16->4, the regularizer stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0); predict val_ssim > 0.84. FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the leanest regularizer, then hammernik_2017 (and the whole VN family -- the sibling hammernik_vn is exhausting capacity + DC weight + filter-normalization in parallel) is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on real 2304-view rebinned Mayo LDCT regardless of regularizer config -> FILE THE NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik learned-regularizer family does not beat LD-FBP on Mayo. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): FEWER filters means CHEAPER per-step compute (conv over 4 instead of 16 channels + 4-channel RBF-bump loop), so wall <= iter-3 (895.8s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, >900s margin. MEMORY-SAFE and strictly LIGHTER than iter-3: batch_size=2 KEPT (do NOT raise: bs=4 OOMed the 16GB RTX5000 in the _rho_prime RBF-bump loop at iter-1), and N_k 16->4 further shrinks the (B,F,H,W) activation tensors held across 5 unrolled steps. grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability).

rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=True, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). LAST-LEVER / confirmation iter. ONE KNOB on the REGULARIZER (not capacity, not lambda): vn_normalize_filters False -> True (constrain each learned filter K_i to zero-mean + unit-norm, the paper-faithful constraint, solver _effective_weight lines 119-128). All else held at iter-3 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_lambda_init=0.05, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS, all hr=0, all BELOW the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, capacity UP -> REGRESSED -0.0133, elapsed 1351.7s); iter-3 SSIM 0.768197 (vn_lambda_init 0.0023->0.05, DC-weight ~22x UP -> REGRESSED -0.0238, elapsed 1159.6s, val_psnr 32.07, val_rmse 1.246e-3). BOTH structural levers already attacked the wrong thing: capacity-UP regressed AND DC-weight-UP regressed, so the recon sits monotonically BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). FAILURE MODE (well-characterized): the learned VN regulariser term Sum_i K_i^T rho'_i(K_i u) is a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline, and it does so REGARDLESS of capacity (filters^ hurt) or DC weight (lambda^ hurt). This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture). Unit-norm caps each filter's gain so no single filter can dominate and over-smooth. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation was the unconstrained filters collapsing to a DC/low-pass smoother, this constraint removes that failure path -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init and hr should rise toward / above 0. HYPOTHESIS: with zero-mean unit-norm filters the regulariser stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0). FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the regulariser CONSTRAINED, then hammernik_vn is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on rebinned Mayo regardless of regulariser config (capacity, DC weight, AND filter constraint all exhausted) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik-VN learned-regulariser family does not beat LD-FBP on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and drive the remaining iters to document the ceiling, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the zero-mean/unit-norm normalization is a cheap per-step reshape (filter tensor is (24,1,11,11)); per-step forward/back-project DC cost is IDENTICAL to iter-3, so wall ~= iter-3 (1159.6s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-3 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB RTX5000 (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM at 72s). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise).

This FIRES iter-3's own pre-registered falsifier: 'if SSIM stays <=0.84 under strong DC, the VN regulariser is structurally degrading -> iter-4 attacks the regulariser itself: vn_normalize_filters=True OR vn_init=backproj'. CHOICE OF KNOB (most diagnostic remaining): vn_normalize_filters=True is the SHARPEST test of the smoothing diagnosis, and is preferred over vn_init=backproj (which changes only the init, not the regularizer mechanism, and the baseline is pinned to FBP either way). MECHANISM: zero-mean filters have NO DC response -- conv with a zero-mean kernel annihilates any uniform/low-frequency level component -- so a zero-mean-unit-norm-constrained K_i CANNOT apply a uniform smoothing or level shift to the image; the regulariser term can only act on local CONTRAST (edges/texture). Unit-norm caps each filter's gain so no single filter can dominate and over-smooth. If the iter-1/2/3 degradation was the unconstrained filters collapsing to a DC/low-pass smoother, this constraint removes that failure path -> the recon should stop sinking below the FBP init and hr should rise toward / above 0. HYPOTHESIS: with zero-mean unit-norm filters the regulariser stops smoothing the FBP init below baseline; val_ssim clears the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr > 0). FALSIFIER (the terminal one): if val_ssim still <= 0.84 (below FBP) with the regulariser CONSTRAINED, then hammernik_vn is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED on rebinned Mayo regardless of regulariser config (capacity, DC weight, AND filter constraint all exhausted) -> file the NEGATIVE RESULT: the Hammernik-VN learned-regulariser family does not beat LD-FBP on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and drive the remaining iters to document the ceiling, not chase it. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the zero-mean/unit-norm normalization is a cheap per-step reshape (filter tensor is (24,1,11,11)); per-step forward/back-project DC cost is IDENTICAL to iter-3, so wall ~= iter-3 (1159.6s) -- well under the 1800s SLURM kill, ~640s margin. rationale: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=3, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.02, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, naf). SIX-BOX. (1) NUMBERS trajectory (monotone climb via leanness, all hr=0): iter-1 naf_hidden=128,layers=4 -> SSIM 0.4729 (PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08, elapsed 1097s, median ~91 Adam steps/scene at the 5.0s per-scene wall, 18-min outer wall 1080s hit EXACTLY at scene 214). iter-2 naf_hidden 128->64 -> SSIM 0.4943 (+0.0215; PSNR 18.62, elapsed 1100s). iter-3 naf_layers 4->3 -> SSIM 0.5452 (+0.0509; PSNR 19.238, RMSE 0.005459, hr 0.005, elapsed 1094.6s, params 0.006465M). Each leanness step (cheaper MLP -> more Adam steps/scene in the FIXED 214x5.0s/18-min wall) lifts SSIM, but STILL FAR below the LD-FBP cal floor (~0.81). (2) FAILURE MODE: budget-starved per-scene INR fit + weak inductive bias for dense 2304-view CT -- climbing but bounded; ~90-100 Adam steps/scene leaves the NeRF-style coordinate-MLP barely off its water-mu init (a NeRF wants hundreds-to-thousands of steps). (3) ONE KNOB: naf_lr 1e-2->2e-2 (naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=3, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). The two LEANNESS levers are now nearly spent: naf_hidden hit 64 (iter-2) and naf_layers hit 3 (iter-3) -- one block left; layers 3->2 would zero the range(layers-2) hidden loop, collapsing to a single Linear(in,64)->Linear(64,1) perceptron (capacity cliff, triggers the lost-capacity falsifier), and naf_n_freqs->6 trades positional-encoding bandwidth (representational power) for a small first-layer saving. naf_lr is the ORTHOGONAL lever that directly attacks the diagnosed too-few-steps-off-init failure WITHOUT further shrinking the fixed model: with only ~90-100 Adam steps from the water-mu init, a 2x lr lets the INR travel further per step (init-anchored Adam, the same regime where iter-1's per-scene rationale already used lr 5e-3->1e-2). Model held fixed so the SSIM delta isolates lr cleanly. 2x (not 5x) is a measured step to avoid destabilizing the short Adam fit. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if naf_lr 1e-2->2e-2, SSIM rises above 0.5452 because each of the ~90-100 per-scene steps moves the INR further off init within the same per-scene wall. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stalls at ~0.54 (or drops from lr-induced instability) despite the higher lr, NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT) and the per-scene-INR fit has hit its ceiling far below FBP (~0.55 vs ~0.81 cal) -> document the per-scene-INR ceiling on dense Mayo as a NEGATIVE result. (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min, in-solver outer wall = governor) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap so the WALL governs, not the iter count). 214 x 5.0s = 1070s ~= the 1080s/18-min outer wall (hit exactly at scene 214 every iter). val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=2, img_n_bf=3, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=5, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, lr=0.005, epochs=24, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the iter-2 BEST config (proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, 12 params, hr 0.0282) -- NOT iter-3's regressed img_n_bf=6 (which collapsed hr to 0.0). ONE KNOB: proj_n_bf 1->2 (projection-domain bilateral DEPTH -- the UNTRIED domain). params 3*(proj_n_bf+img_n_bf) = 3*(2+3) = 15 (up from iter-2's 12; iter-3's image-domain bump went to 21 and REGRESSED). epochs KEPT at 24 (proven inert iter-1->iter-2), img_n_bf KEPT at 3 (the iter-2 best, NOT iter-3's 6), all sigmas/kernels/lr/grad_clip identical to iter-2. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 SSIM 0.919181 hr 0.027984 in 254.3s @ ep8, 12 params (params_M 1.2e-05); iter-2 SSIM 0.919155 hr 0.028237 in 449.6s @ ep24, 12 params -- the BEST; FLAT vs iter-1 (epochs INERT, +0.0003 = noise); iter-3 SSIM 0.905690 hr 0.0 in 574.3s @ img_n_bf=6, 21 params -- REGRESSED (image-domain capacity++ DESTABILIZED, hr collapsed 0.0282->0.0). (2) FAILURE MODE: few-param dual-domain trainable-bilateral at a CAPACITY CEILING (~hr 0.028) on the 2304-view Mayo FBP. Two levers are SPENT: epochs is inert (iter-1->iter-2 flat), and image-domain capacity-up HURTS (iter-3 regressed to 0). The remaining UNTRIED lever is the OTHER domain -- the projection-domain bilateral, which has been FROZEN at proj_n_bf=1 for all 3 prior iters. (3) ONE KNOB = proj_n_bf 1->2. JUSTIFICATION vs the other iter-4 candidate (img_kernel 5->7, named by iter-3's falsifier): img_kernel-up adds IMAGE-domain smoothing/receptive-field -- the SAME domain whose capacity bump (img_n_bf 3->6) just REGRESSED hr to 0.0 in iter-3 -- so it probes the proven-harmful direction. proj_n_bf-up instead attacks the genuinely untested projection domain: a 2nd sinogram-domain bilateral cleans correlated projection noise BEFORE the 2304-view FBP adjoint amplifies it, a fundamentally different denoising locus than the post-FBP image domain. This is the cleaner falsification of iter-3's structural-ceiling claim (does ANY domain's capacity move hr, or only image-domain that destabilizes?). PARAM COUNT: 12->15 (+3, one extra 3-param bilateral) -- a MODEST add, far below iter-3's 21 that regressed; the image domain stays at the iter-2 best img_n_bf=3 so the image-domain instability is NOT re-triggered. (4) HYPOTHESIS: a 2nd projection-domain bilateral (15 vs 12 params) lifts hr above 0.028237 because cleaning sinogram noise pre-FBP attacks the noise where the FBP adjoint has not yet correlated/amplified it -- a locus the inert epochs and the destabilizing image-domain depth could not reach. FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=0.029 (flat or regression at proj_n_bf=2), the dual-domain trainable-bilateral is STRUCTURALLY capped on Mayo regardless of WHICH domain's capacity is increased (image-domain regressed in iter-3, projection-domain inert here) -> FILE THE CEILING VERDICT: the ~hr 0.028 ceiling is the few-param-bilateral structural limit on real 2304-view Mayo LDCT, and no within-architecture knob escapes it. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score. iter-2 @ ep24, 12 params ran in 449.6s; per-step cost is dominated by the SHARED 2304-view FBP adjoint, NOT the bilateral params, so adding ONE projection-domain BF (1->2) costs only one extra cheap sinogram-bilateral pass per step -> est ~460-520s, comfortably <1200s. val_n=214 KEPT (do NOT reduce), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT, epochs=24 KEPT. sbatch --time=00:30:00 = SLURM safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned.
