rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.001, tv_iterations=160, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). BASE = the iter-2 BEST config (clip 0.08, lambda 0.001), NOT iter-3's regressed lambda 0.003. ONE KNOB: tv_iterations 120->160 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_lambda=0.001, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). TRAJECTORY (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05, 120 iters, 918s); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08, 120 iters, 928.5s) -- the BEST, #4 overall on Mayo; iter-3 SSIM 0.919984 hr 0.136636 RMSE 8.536e-4 (lambda 0.001->0.003, 120 iters, 923.9s) -- REGRESSED, over-smoothed (lambda-up is exhausted). The two prior levers are SPENT: tv_clip_max is at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] (clip exhausted), and tv_lambda-up regressed in iter-3 (denoise-strength exhausted). The remaining untried lever is tv_iterations: it has been FROZEN at 120 for all 3 prior iters, deliberately conservative to protect the 20-min wall. OPPORTUNITY: is hr 0.205 ITERATIONS-LIMITED (the TV gradient descent has not fully converged at 120 steps, so the recon still has residual data-term error the schedule has not driven out) or is it at the TV REGULARIZATION CEILING (120 iters is already converged and 0.205 hr / ~0.924 SSIM is the structural TV limit on real Mayo LDCT)? FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: oversizing tv_iterations blows the HARD 20-min (1200s) wall on the 214-slice val pass. HYPOTHESIS: 33% more TV gradient-descent steps (120->160) from the iter-2 BEST config converge the recon further, lowering val_rmse below 7.857e-4 so hr rises above 0.205364 (the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower residual). FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression at 160 iters), TV is at its regularization ceiling on Mayo (~0.924 SSIM / 0.205 hr) and 120 iters was already converged -- the iters lever is exhausted too, and the next probe would be tv_lr (finer convergence per step) or accept the structural TV ceiling. BUDGET: the cost model is T(n)=overhead + n*c_step. From iter-2's 928.5s at 120 iters and the iter-1 per-slice-iter rate (~0.018 s/slice-iter * 214 slices = 3.85 s/TV-iter), fixed overhead (214-slice load+FBP+per-iter scoring) ~= 466s. n=160 -> T ~= 466 + 160*3.85 ~= 1083s = 90% of the 1200s budget (~117s margin). Robustness: even at +10% step-cost variance (GPU contention) n=160 lands ~1144s, still under the wall; n=180 was REJECTED because at +10% variance it goes over (1229s). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged (do NOT reduce). sbatch --time=00:30:00 gives a SLURM-level safety net above the 20-min metric-validity budget.

LIMITER = now WALL-LIMITED on epochs, NOT capacity. SSIM is still climbing on epochs (iter-1 iters5/ep6 0.84271 @1149.5s; iter-2 iters3/ep10 0.863635 @1079.3s=17.99min; iter-3 iters3/ep11 0.885115 @1213.6s=20.23min) BUT iter-3 OVERSHOT the HARD 1200s/20-min budget: true marginal epoch cost = 1213.6-1079.3 = 134.3 s/epoch (higher than iter-3's 107.9s estimate), so ep12 would land ~1348s=22.5min, well over the wall. Epochs cannot go up. Per the no-trade-epochs-for-capacity rule, lpd_hidden^ and lpd_iters^ are also OFF (both add per-sample projector fwd+adj cost and blow the wall; iter-1 at iters=5 already hit 19.16min). The remaining wall-NEUTRAL lever is lr: at the budget-capped epoch count, a higher lr lets the cosine schedule traverse more of the loss landscape per epoch, extracting more training progress WITHOUT buying epochs or capacity. lr 7e-4 (NOT 6e-4: the prior run flagged lr~6e-4 as an ANOMALOUS COLLAPSE point; 7e-4 was a stable trained 0.9638 point) is the safe lr-up step. Epochs set back to 10 (iter-2's count, ran 1079.3s=18.0min, safely inside 1200s) to RESTORE the budget margin iter-3 broke. BUDGET MATH vs 1200s: iter-2 ran 1079.3s at ep10 -> iter-4 at the same ep10 + lr-only change is compute-identical (lr does not change FLOPs) => ~1079s=18.0min, well inside the 20-min wall. HYP: at the budget-capped ep10, lr 7e-4 extracts more SSIM per epoch than 5e-4 (faster cosine traversal), lifting SSIM toward clearing the LD-FBP floor (hr>0); predict ~0.87-0.89. FALSIFIER: SSIM <= 0.885115 (iter-3) OR flat/down with hr still 0.000 => LPD has hit its budget-constrained ceiling on 2304-view Mayo (~0.885 SSIM, hr 0); neither epochs (wall-capped) nor lr is the lever -> projector-in-loop LPD is structurally FBP-bounded at this capacity/budget (documented ceiling), and iter-5 would need a deeper wall, not more of this budget.

rationale: uswin-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=214, epochs=34, batch_size=4, lr=0.0005, uswin_c=32, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=900, seed=42, rationale=ITER-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). ONE KNOB: CAPACITY uswin_c 24 -> 32 (every encoder level widens c, 2c, 4c, 8c; the WindowMSA at each level runs MHA on the wider dim with heads HELD at 4 -> head_dim = 32/4 = 8 valid, 24/4=6 before; uswin_c=32 is in the sanctioned TPE search space [16,24,32]; params ~3.95M -> ~6.9M, a (32/24)^2 = 1.778x conv+attention compute bump), with epochs TRADED DOWN 64 -> 34 to fit the HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score wall. This is the same capacity-for-epochs trade the champion dual_domain_supervised just ran (c16->24, ep27->10). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) TRAJECTORY iter-1 ep10 c24 -> SSIM 0.885910 / hr 0.173021 in 328.96s; iter-2 ep40 c24 -> SSIM 0.914097 / hr 0.322063 in 737.72s; iter-3 ep64 c24 -> SSIM 0.924443 / hr 0.353196 in 1085.87s (CURRENT, #2 on the Mayo board). current config uswin_c=24 epochs=64. (2) LIMITER: the epochs lever is now BOTH wall-locked AND showing diminishing returns. WALL: iter-3 ep64 used 1085.87s = 90.5pct of the 1200s budget; the iter-3 note computed ep72 -> 1174s = 19.6 min (only 26s margin), so epochs cannot meaningfully rise. DIMINISHING RETURNS: hr gained +0.149 over ep10->40 (+30 ep) but only +0.031 over ep40->64 (+24 ep) -> the per-epoch hr slope is flattening, the c24 net is approaching its training-convergence basin. iter-3's OWN falsifier named this exact pivot: 'if hr plateaus ... iter-4 must raise uswin_c (24->32)'. The new lever is CAPACITY, not epochs. (3) ONE KNOB: uswin_c 24->32, epochs 64->34; ALL else held (train_n=200, val_n=214, bs=4, lr=5e-4, swin_window=8, swin_heads=4, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). BUDGET-TRADE MATH (worst-case-sized, mirroring the champion's method): from the two measured c24 (epochs, elapsed_s) points (40,737.72),(64,1085.87): per_epoch_c24 = (1085.87-737.72)/(64-40) = 14.51 s/epoch; fixed_c24 (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure I/O) = 737.72 - 40*14.51 = 157.3s (predicts ep64 = 157.3 + 64*14.51 = 1086.0s vs actual 1085.87 -> calibration exact). A c24->c32 widening multiplies the U-Net+attention compute by (32/24)^2 = 1.778x; the per-sample 2304-view FBP adjoint is c-INDEPENDENT. WORST CASE (pessimistically assume EVERYTHING incl. the FBP adjoint scales 1.778x): per_epoch_worst = 14.51*1.778 = 25.80 s/epoch; fixed_worst = 157.3*1.778 = 279.7s. Largest epoch count fitting 1200s: (1200-279.7)/25.80 = 35.7 -> ep34 worst-case = 279.7 + 34*25.80 = 1156.9s = 19.3 min (43s margin inside the 1200s budget; sbatch wall is 30 min). ep36 worst-case = 1208.5s BUSTS the budget, so ep34 is the LARGEST epoch count guaranteed to fit even the worst case; epochs is sized to the worst-case bound, not the optimistic one (a wall-bust wastes the whole QOS slot). REALISTIC (FBP adjoint ~30pct of per-epoch, c-independent): per_epoch_real = 14.51*(0.30+0.70*1.778) = 22.42 s/epoch -> ep34 real ~ 243 + 34*22.42 = 1005s = 16.7 min, comfortable headroom. Train-only worst = 34*25.80 = 877s < max_train_s=900 backstop (set to 900 so train always halts leaving >=300s for the worst-case val+figure inside the 1200s budget; iter-3 used 1000 but the bigger net's fixed-cost grew, so 900 is the safe backstop). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 1.778x more representational capacity lifts hr above the iter-3 0.353196 toward/past the champion dual_domain_supervised's 0.365, even at the reduced ep34, because uswin's hr is flattening at c24 (training-basin) yet remains a strong Mayo image-domain denoiser and c32 is its top sanctioned capacity. Predicted iter-4 hr ~0.36-0.38. FALSIFIER (NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.353196 at uswin_c=32/ep34, uswin has hit its representational ceiling on this val set (~0.355) AND/OR ep34 under-trained the bigger net more than the added capacity helped -> iter-5 either (a) keeps c32 and recovers epochs toward the wall if the measured c32 per-epoch is cheaper than the 25.80s worst case (i.e. ep34 left budget headroom), or (b) reverts to c24/ep64 and accepts 0.3532 as the uswin ceiling. (5) HARD 20-min train+score budget; val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices (NOT reduced); grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint amplifies gradients). HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). (6) no control return.

rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=60, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-3 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 400->60 (per-scene Adam steps DOWN to MAXIMIZE completed-scene COVERAGE; all other knobs held at iter-2). FAILURE MODE (the core, structural problem): R2-Gaussian is a PER-SCENE Gaussian-splatting fit (no training) and is BUDGET-INCOMPATIBLE with the 214-slice Mayo protocol at a hard 20-min wall. Measured per-scene step cost is a clean linear function of gs_n_iter: iter-1 (n_iter=150) = 42.45 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 26/214 (12% coverage), SSIM 0.738335, hr=0; iter-2 (n_iter=400) = 113.0 s/scene -> outer-wall hit at sample 10/214 (4.7% coverage), SSIM 0.736981, hr=0. Linear fit: 0.2822 s/Adam-step (offset ~0). iter-2 FALSIFIER FIRED: the hypothesis 'more Adam steps lifts per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738' is REFUTED -- 2.67x more steps (150->400) moved the average-over-214 SSIM by -0.0001 (0.7383 -> 0.7370, FLAT). So per-scene quality is NOT the lever; the average is dominated by the ~95% of scenes that NEVER complete (scored at/near their FBP init). DIAGNOSTIC QUESTION for iter-3: does COVERAGE win? At gs_n_iter=60 -> per-scene = 0.2822*60 = 16.9 s -> 1080s outer wall / 16.9 = ~64/214 scenes complete (30% coverage, ~2.5x iter-1's 26, ~6.4x iter-2's 10). HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): if the average-over-214 SSIM goes UP at 64-scene coverage (vs 0.738 @ 26 scenes and 0.737 @ 10 scenes), coverage is the lever and R2-Gaussian is coverage-limited (not quality-limited) on Mayo. FALSIFIER: if average-over-214 SSIM stays ~0.74 or WORSE even at 2.5x coverage, then BOTH levers (per-scene quality AND coverage) are exhausted within the 20-min budget -> R2-Gaussian is STRUCTURALLY budget-incompatible with the 214-slice Mayo protocol -> file the quality-vs-coverage tradeoff as a documented NEGATIVE RESULT (no gs_n_iter both covers all 214 AND fits per-scene: covering all 214 in 1080s needs n_iter<=18 steps, which is a non-recon). BUDGET MATH: 64 scenes * 16.9 s = 1082s ~ the 1080s outer wall (self-truncates and scores whatever completed, exactly as iter-1/iter-2); SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, val figure excluded. val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced) per mandate; gs_n_gaussians held at 512 (<=1024 cap). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.7383 (26/214) -> iter-2 0.7370 (10/214) -> iter-3 predicted ~0.74-0.76 if coverage helps (64/214), or ~0.74 (structural negative) if it does not.

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-05, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). RE-DIAGNOSIS from the iter-3 SLURM LOG (job 765340), which contradicts the iter-3 observation narrative: the 0.2855->0.8137 jump was NOT training un-freezing -- it is the LD-FBP PASSTHROUGH. Log facts: loss=0.000064 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs (did NOT decrease); lambda[k]=0.001 STILL PINNED at init for all 8 epochs (zero gradient); step[k] crept only 1.06e-8->1.76e-8. At tv_step_init=1e-8 the unrolled update f = f - step*(data_grad + lam*tv_grad) is scaled to ~zero, so the K=30 unroll is a near-identity map on fbp_init: pred ~= clamp(LD-FBP). That is why SSIM=0.8137 ~= the LD-FBP floor (~0.81), recon PSNR 33.60 is JUST BELOW baseline_PSNR 34.08, and hr=0.0 (the recon does not beat its own FBP). The freeze did not get fixed -- it MOVED: iter-1/2 (step=1e-2) froze via SATURATED-CLAMP (overshoot clamps the whole image, clamp derivative 0); iter-3 (step=1e-8) freezes via VANISHING-STEP (data+TV terms scaled to nothing, lam has no effect on the output so d loss/d lam ~= 0). FAILURE MODE (named): the limiter is the STEP SCALE, not depth (tv_K falsified iter-1->2) and not epochs/lr (lr=5e-2 already; scalars still don't move because the gradient to lambda is ~0 at both step extremes). The working step lives BETWEEN the two known-frozen regimes 1e-8 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-8 -> 1e-5 (the geometric midpoint sqrt(1e-8*1e-2)=1e-5 of the two frozen endpoints). At ~1e-5 the data-consistency term back_project(Rf-sino) actually moves the image OFF the FBP init across K=30 steps (so the recon depends on lambda -> non-zero gradient reaches log_lambda -> the 30 TV scalars can finally train), while staying INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin (no whole-image saturation -> the clamp derivative is not 0 -> gradient also reaches log_step). Everything else IDENTICAL to iter-3 (lr=5e-2, K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-6, val_n=214 ALL L277, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0; tv_step_init STAYS finite/non-tiny -- do NOT revert toward 1e-8). HYPOTHESIS: with the step in the active basin, training un-freezes for REAL this time -- loss DECREASES across epochs, lambda[k] DEPARTS from 0.001 and step[k] adapts, and SSIM rises ABOVE the 0.8137 FBP passthrough toward the classical TV band (SSIM 0.85-0.92, the non-trained tv_iterative sibling hits 0.92 / hr 0.205); clearing hr>0 means the trained TV recon finally beats its own LD-FBP. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.81 with lambda STILL pinned (passthrough persists, the active basin is even narrower than 1e-5) OR collapses back toward ~0.286 (1e-5 already over-saturates the clamp), then the supervised-TV harness has NO step value that both trains the scalars AND beats FBP under Mayo's 2304-view unnormalized-adjoint scale within the config-only contract (the shared solver's raw back_project step is FORBIDDEN to edit) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is FBP-bounded on real Mayo LDCT) and STOP iterating this solver; iter-5 would only bracket the step further (e.g. 3e-6 / 3e-5) before declaring the negative. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score = 1200s wall): IDENTICAL compute to iter-3 (same K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, val_n=214, val_chunk=5 -- only the init VALUE of a scalar changes, not any loop size) -> ~918s measured iter-3, ~282s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 0.8137 (FBP passthrough, hr 0) -> iter-4 either >0.84 with lambda departing init and hr>0 (training un-froze for real) OR ~0.81 with lambda still pinned (passthrough -> bracket once at iter-5 then NEGATIVE RESULT + STOP).

rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_constrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_constrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=1.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=5, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=0.3, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-3 search-20260619-01 CONSTRAINED diff-recon. ONE KNOB: recon_dcstep_relax 1.0->0.3 (the constrained-specific hard-CG blend; eta held at iter-2's 1.0). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 eta=30 SSIM 0.3937/hr0; iter-2 eta 30->1 REGRESSED to SSIM 0.2366/hr0 -> eta is the WRONG lever (gentling the DPS gain did not help; the corruption is elsewhere). FAILURE MODE (numbers): both prior iters ran recon_dcstep_relax=1.0 = FULL hard projection. In dc_step_cg() the return is relax*x_cg + (1-relax)*x0_mu; relax=1.0 discards the diffusion x0 estimate ENTIRELY and substitutes n_cg=3 Gauss-Newton least-squares fit to the NOISY 2304-view LD sinogram, which is then re-noised back to t_next every 5 reverse steps (warmup 5). That least-squares fit overfits measurement noise and overwrites the prior's structure -> hard-CG DC re-noises a corrupted x0, exactly the constrained variant's failure. The SOLVER DEFAULT is relax=0.5; relax=1.0 was an untested aggressive choice carried from iter-1. ONE KNOB: relax 1.0->0.3 blends 30% CG-projected + 70% diffusion x0, a GENTLE pull to data consistency that preserves prior structure instead of overwriting it. rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_unconstrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=32, recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=0, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-3 search-20260619-01 UNCONSTRAINED diff-recon vs reused Mayo DDPM v4 ckpt (ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt). ONE KNOB: recon_sample_steps (n_steps) 25 -> 32 (LONGER DDIM reverse trajectory). All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_dcstep_every=0 so the hard-CG projection stays OFF -> pure soft DPS; recon_eta_clamp=false; val_n=214). TRAJECTORY iter-1 (n_steps=25, eta=30): SSIM 0.3688, hr=0.0, PSNR 10.55, 868.65s/214 = 4.06 s/slice. iter-2 (n_steps=25, eta=5): SSIM 0.3960, hr=0.0, PSNR 11.25, 868.33s/214 = 4.06 s/slice. The eta 30->5 correction gave a SLIGHT lift (+0.027) but the recon is STILL FAR below the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 (and the constrained sibling REGRESSED on its eta fix eta30->1: 0.39->0.24), so the DPS guidance-gain lever is now EXHAUSTED. FAILURE MODE: the recon is dominated by a Mayo v4 DDPM prior that is MISMATCHED to the rebinned-Mayo distribution under the short 25-step low-T reverse budget -- per findings the prior is globally faithful (plausible CT texture) but NOT conditionally faithful to the input sino under DPS/DC (exactly the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict, where 4x-16x capacity + 2.5x training all stayed in the 0.3-0.5 SSIM band). ONE KNOB JUSTIFICATION: n_steps is the highest-value untried lever -- a longer DDIM reverse trajectory gives the soft-DPS prior more steps to settle from the FBP init toward the measurement manifold; the 25-step low-T budget may simply be too short to converge. BUDGET MATH (HARD 20-min = 1200s wall, val=ALL 214 L277 slices): per-step cost dominates (each of the n_steps reverse iterations does one DDPM-net forward + one projector forward + one autograd backward; dcstep_every=0 so NO extra CG cost), so per-slice cost is ~linear in n_steps with a small fixed FBP-init+IO offset. iter-2 = 4.06 s/slice at 25 steps. At 32 steps (worst-case fully-linear): 4.06*(32/25) = 5.20 s/slice -> 214*5.20 = 1112s = 18.5 min < 1200s wall (~88s headroom, MORE in practice because the fixed offset does not scale). Doubling to 50 steps (8.1 s/slice -> ~29 min) would BLOW the wall, so n_steps=32 (+28% trajectory) is the LARGEST step count that fits with margin -- the right budget-feasible probe, not a naive 2x. HYPOTHESIS: if I extend the DDIM trajectory 25 -> 32 steps, SSIM rises meaningfully above the iter-2 0.3960 because the longer reverse path lets the FBP-initialized iterate relax further onto the sino-consistent mode. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays well below the FBP floor (~0.4 vs 0.81) even with the longer trajectory, then the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is STRUCTURALLY mismatched (not a step-budget issue) -> file a negative result and STOP iterating diffusion-recon on Mayo (the lever is the prior CLASS, not any sampler hyperparameter, mirroring the breast-DDPM decision).

rationale: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=64, naf_layers=3, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-3 (search-20260619-01, naf). SIX-BOX. (1) NUMBERS trajectory: iter-1 naf_hidden=128 -> SSIM 0.4729, hr 0.0, PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08, elapsed 1097s, median ~91 Adam steps/scene (5.0s per-scene wall), 18-min outer wall (1080s) hit EXACTLY at scene 214 (1082.5s). iter-2 naf_hidden=128->64 (cheaper hiddenxhidden matmuls -> more steps/scene) -> SSIM 0.4943, hr 0.0, PSNR 18.62, elapsed 1100s: +0.0215 SSIM, CONFIRMING the budget-starvation diagnosis (cheaper step -> more per-scene optimization -> higher SSIM). Still FAR below the LD-FBP floor (~0.81 cal). (2) FAILURE MODE: budget-starved per-scene INR fit. A NeRF-style coordinate-MLP wants hundreds-to-thousands of Adam steps to leave its water-mu init; ~91 steps/scene at hidden=128 (more at hidden=64) leaves the INR barely off init. iter-2's +0.0215 proves we are still on the starvation slope, NOT yet at the structural floor. (3) ONE KNOB: naf_layers 4->3 (naf_hidden=64, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). The hidden-width lever was spent in iter-2; the next leanness step is MLP DEPTH. NAF.__init__ builds [Linear(in,h),ReLU] + (layers-2) x [Linear(h,h),ReLU] + Linear(h,1); at layers=4 that is TWO hiddenxhidden blocks, at layers=3 it is ONE -> removing one full 64x64 Linear+ReLU cuts the per-step MLP matmul cost ~1/3 (over 512^2=262144 coords each step) on top of the fixed 2304-view fan-beam forward+backward. 214-SCENE 20-MIN BUDGET MATH (measured): train_n=0, the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop; total = 214 x per_scene_s = 214 x 5.0s = 1070s ~= the 1080s/18-min outer wall, hit exactly at scene 214 (verified both iters). I CANNOT raise per_scene_s (214 x wall already fills the 20-min compute budget). So to buy MORE Adam steps per scene at FIXED 214x1080s total I make each step CHEAPER again: layers 4->3 drops one 64x64 block -> more steps fit in each 5.0s scene within the SAME wall. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I shrink naf_layers 4->3, I expect SSIM to rise above 0.4943 because the shallower MLP buys more Adam steps per scene, letting the INR move further off its water-mu init within the same per-scene wall (same mechanism that gave iter-2 +0.0215). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stalls at ~0.49 (or drops) despite the extra steps, NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT) AND/OR has lost too much MLP capacity to represent the slice -> document the per-scene-INR ceiling on dense Mayo as a NEGATIVE result (SSIM ~0.5 vs LD-FBP ~0.81). (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min, in-solver outer wall = governor) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap so the WALL governs, not the iter count), val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

rationale: itnet-claude-agentic: pretrain_epochs=160, pretrain_lr=0.0001, itnet_k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, finetune_epochs=0, finetune_lr=0.0001, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric) for itnet = ItNet v1 (pretrain-denoiser-then-FIXED-DC, solver_itnet.py). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR RESULTS: iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.4413 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 20.44 / RMSE 0.004756, elapsed 191.1s; iter-2 ep48 -> SSIM 0.5927 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 24.77 / RMSE 0.002886, elapsed 387.4s. The pretrain_epochs lever moves SSIM (0.4413->0.5927, +0.151 over 8->48 ep) but hr stays PINNED at 0.000 -- v1 is still BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor after a 6x pretrain increase. CONTRAST: the lever-twin itnet_v2 (same pretrain-then-DC family) climbed ep48 0.5888 -> ep144 0.6230 (3x epochs for only +0.034 SSIM, hr still 0.000 -- severe diminishing returns), while the END-TO-END-trained sibling itnet_v3 sits at 0.905 / hr 0.312 at iter-3. v1 (0.44->0.59) and v2 (0.59->0.62) trace the SAME under-0.81 curve; v3 (0.91) is on a different curve entirely. (2) LIMITER = the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC CEILING (structural, confirmed by reading solver_itnet.py): finetune_itnet() is DEFINED (lines 114-135) but NEVER called in main(); the k=3 ItNet DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable parameters of its own (self.alpha is a plain float, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN); itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() (lines 208-209) run the unroll as pure INFERENCE. The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M=0.2329, exactly the UNet), pretrained as an FBP->truth denoiser that NEVER sees the DC steps during training. So pretrain_epochs is the sole lever and the fixed untrained DC post-processor caps v1 far below the end-to-end v3. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48 -> 160 (3.3x), mirroring v2's 48->144 ceiling-probe escalation. All else identical to iter-2 (k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, pretrain_lr=1e-4, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: a final hard push of the only trainable component. FALSIFIER (the operative one): if SSIM stays well below the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor and far below v3's 0.91 (predicted ~0.63-0.66, tracking v2's flattening 0.62 at comparable epochs), itnet v1 is STRUCTURALLY pretrain-then-fixed-DC-capped -- NOT under-trained -- and the campaign should document this ceiling and direct future Mayo recon to itnet_v3 (end-to-end unrolled, 0.91) rather than spend more iters on v1's epochs lever. The counter-hypothesis (v1 suddenly clears 0.81 at 160 ep) is implausible given the +0.151 then +0.034-class diminishing slope already measured. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): from the two measured points the per-epoch pretrain cost is (387.4-191.1)/(48-8) = 4.91 s/epoch and the fixed cost (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup) is 191.1 - 8*4.91 = 151.8 s. pretrain_epochs=160 predicts 151.8 + 160*4.91 = 937 s = 15.6 min, comfortably inside the 1200s budget with margin for val-pass variance; pretrain_epochs=200 would predict 1134s (18.9 min, too tight), so 160 is a safe decisive push. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside the DC step overflows otherwise). v1 has NO max_train_s backstop (not in the solver), so the 30-min sbatch wall is the only hard fence -- 15.6 min predicted leaves ample headroom. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each val slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override).

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.05, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=1e-08, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). TRAINING-DIAGNOSIS iter, NOT a hyperparameter tune. PRIOR: iter-1 (K=10) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 321.5s; iter-2 (K=30) SSIM 0.285541 hr 0.0 PSNR 1.87 elapsed 946s -- BYTE-IDENTICAL to every digit, comparison.png identical (289606 B). iter-2 deepened the unroll 10->30 and the result did NOT change AT ALL -> depth is FALSIFIED as the limiter. SLURM TRAINING LOG (jobs 765204 iter-1 / 765283 iter-2) shows the smoking gun: loss=0.001739 IDENTICAL across all 8 epochs, and the learnable step[k]=0.01, lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init for all 8 epochs -- the 20/60 scalars receive ZERO gradient and never move. FAILURE MODE (named): the supervised TV TRAINING is structurally frozen by a SATURATED-CLAMP gradient kill. Mechanism: data_grad = back_project(Rf - sino) is the RAW unfiltered adjoint of a 2304-view Mayo sinogram (sum-scaled, NO 1/N normalization). The classical tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92) computes its gradient via AUTOGRAD on 0.5*mean(residual^2) -- a mean over 2304*736~1.7e6 elements -> per-element gradient ~1.7e6x SMALLER. tv_step_init=0.01 was inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr but the supervised path's gradient is ~1.7e6x bigger, so f - 0.01*data_grad overshoots massively -> clamp(0,0.05) saturates the WHOLE image at K=1 -> the saturated clamp has derivative 0 everywhere -> no gradient reaches log_step/log_lambda -> scalars frozen, recon a near-constant clamped blob (PSNR 1.87, RMSE 0.0403) regardless of K. baseline LD-FBP PSNR=34.08 (Wagner-grade) confirms the data/projector are fine -- only the unrolled step scale is wrong. ONE CHANGE (un-stick training): tv_step_init 0.01 -> 1e-8 (operator-norm-matched: 0.01 / (2304*736) ~ 6e-9, rounded to 1e-8) so the unrolled iteration stays INSIDE the [0,0.05] clamp basin where the clamp is NOT saturated and gradients flow to the scalars. PAIRED ENABLER (not an independent knob -- with frozen gradients lr is inert): outer lr 5e-3 -> 5e-2 so the now-NONZERO scalar gradients move meaningfully across 8 epochs over the log-parametrised step/lambda. All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=30, train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05, val_n=214 ALL L277, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: with the step un-saturated, training un-freezes -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and SSIM rises from 0.2855 toward (and ideally above) the LD-FBP floor (~0.81) / the classical TV ceiling (SSIM 0.92, hr 0.205); even landing near the FBP baseline clears the 0.2855 collapse and proves the harness is repairable. FALSIFIER (decisive): if SSIM stays ~0.286 (clamp still saturates) OR the scalars still don't move, the supervised-TV harness is STRUCTURALLY BROKEN on Mayo's 2304-view scale via the shared solver's unnormalized-adjoint step (which is FORBIDDEN to edit per the no-shared-module rule) -> file a NEGATIVE RESULT (supervised-TV-unrolled is not viable on real Mayo LDCT under the config-only contract) and STOP iterating this solver. BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score): identical compute to iter-2 (K=30, same train/val sizes) -> ~946s, ~250s margin under the 1200s wall; sbatch --time=00:30:00 carries figure/IO headroom. Predicted iter trajectory: iter-1 0.2855 -> iter-2 0.2855 -> iter-3 either >0.81 (training un-froze, harness repaired) OR ~0.286 (structural -> negative result + STOP).

ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48->144 (3x); pretrain_patience tracked 48->144 so early-stop never fires before the full run (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1/iter-2 where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-2 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 960->1100 (18.3-min HARD backstop) to admit the longer pretrain inside the 20-min train+score budget while leaving the figure outside. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=12 in elapsed_s=170.2; iter-2 = SSIM 0.5888 / hr 0.000 @pretrain_epochs=48 in elapsed_s=345.2. Trajectory: 4x epochs (12->48) lifted SSIM +0.133, still hr=0 (FBP floor ~0.81, far above). v3 SIBLING (same ItNet family, END-TO-END unrolled, no pretrain-DC) reaches SSIM 0.91 -- the contrast that frames v2's limiter. Budget: iter-2 used only 345s of the 1200s (20-min) budget (~29%) -- large headroom remains; the variable (pretrain) part was ~233s, fixed (214-slice per-sample val + figure) ~112s. (2) LIMITER: pretrain-DC UNDER-CONVERGENCE -- and structurally deeper: reading solver_itnet_v2.py, the DC stage is NOT trained at all. pretrain_denoiser trains ONLY the SmallUNet on (fbp, truth) residual pairs; ItNetV2 is then built and itnet.eval() runs with NO fine-tune of the unrolled net -- log_alpha (the DC step size) is never optimized, so the k=3 DC refinement is a FIXED, untrained operator wrapped around a pretrained denoiser. That is why v2 caps far below the end-to-end v3 (0.91): more pretraining only sharpens the denoiser, it cannot fix the un-trained DC coupling. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48->144 (3x) -- the most diagnostic single knob to MAP the pretrain-epochs response curve and definitively decide whether the cap is epochs or architecture. Chosen over a DC-stage knob (itnet_k / itnet_alpha_init) because the DC stage carries no trainable weight (changing k/alpha shifts a fixed operator, not a learnable one -- low diagnostic value), and over lr-up (v3 unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe sibling move). With a fixed-DC architecture, pretrain_epochs is the ONLY lever that can lift the denoiser, so pushing it 3x is the cleanest test of the ceiling. (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: if pretrain_epochs 48->144 lands val_ssim still ~0.59-0.65 (NOT the ~0.91 v3 band), then itnet_v2's pretrain-then-FIXED-DC scheme is STRUCTURALLY CAPPED on Mayo regardless of epochs -- the un-trained DC operator, not under-training, is the limiter -- and the campaign should treat v2 as a documented budget/architecture ceiling and use v3 instead. CONVERSELY if SSIM jumps substantially toward the sibling band, the cap was pretrain-epochs and iter-4 keeps climbing. The diminishing 12->48 (+0.133) vs the still-large gap to 0.81/0.91 predicts the former (structural cap). (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. Per-epoch ~4.86s over 200 stratified slices (from iter-1->iter-2 slope) -> 144 ep ~700s pretrain + ~112s fixed val+figure ~812s, comfortably under 1200s and the 30-min sbatch wall; max_train_s=1100 is the HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=4, n_iter=15, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, lr=0.0003, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1080, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=dual_domain_n2i iter-3 (search-20260619-01, PER-IMAGE Noise2Inverse: warm-start pre-pass + per-scan Adam fit; NEVER amortized). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) TRAJECTORY: iter-1 (pretrain_epochs=1, n_iter=15, lr=1e-3) SSIM 0.8622, hr 0, PSNR 33.07, RMSE 1.11e-3, elapsed 972.0s (16.2 min), per-scan 0.264 s/step (214x15 in 846.9s). iter-2 (pretrain_epochs 1->4, lr=1e-3) SSIM 0.8681 (+0.0059), hr 0, PSNR 32.43 (DOWN 0.64), RMSE 1.195e-3 (UP), elapsed 1112.3s (18.5 min). (2) LIMITER (iter-2 falsifier TRIGGERED on the RMSE axis): deepening the warm-start RAISED SSIM but LOWERED PSNR and RAISED RMSE -> the recon moved FURTHER below the 34.08 FBP baseline on the headroom-relevant (RMSE) metric. The SSIM rise is the bilateral-class smoothing artifact (SSIM rewards the smoother deeper denoiser; the calibrated RMSE-sensitive headroom metric does not). So warm-start DEPTH is NOT the binding constraint and is wrong-signed for headroom. Trajectory: iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 hr 0.0 (blend 0.3, factor 0.55); iter-2 SSIM 0.8644 hr EXACTLY 0.0 (blend 0.3->0.5) -- the FBP/RAM blend coefficient is EXHAUSTED: raising the FBP fraction lifted raw SSIM marginally (+0.003) but did NOT move calibrated headroom off 0.0, so on the RMSE-sensitive metric RAM is at/below the LD-FBP floor (baseline 0.8078, oracle HD-FBP 0.9331) regardless of blend. Failure mode: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot deepinv recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned fan data; its denoiser adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense (2304-view) rebinned Mayo -> FBP-bounded. ONE knob NOT yet probed = ram_factor (physics.factor, solver_ram.py L348), the operator-gain used in RAM's prox_l2 data-consistency realign step (L20: 0 = skip prox_l2). It is the most DIAGNOSTIC remaining RAM hyperparameter: blend mixes FBP vs RAM linearly AFTER inference, whereas ram_factor changes RAM's INTERNAL DC step -- the actual mechanism by which RAM is supposed to add signal over its FBP init. Lower it 0.55->0.2 (toward the skip-prox_l2 limit) to isolate whether weakening RAM's DC realign moves the metric at all. Budget: only a scalar physics.factor changes -> zero added compute vs iter-2 (which ran 1100.9 s = 18.3 min for 214 single forward passes + one op-norm power iter), inside the HARD 20-min train+score budget; sbatch --time=00:30:00 backstop wall. val_n stays 214 (score ALL L277 slices @ 321px detector-geometry FOV). rationale: tv_iterative-claude-agentic: val_n=214, train_n=0, tv_lambda=0.003, tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, tv_optimizer=gd, tv_init=fbp, rationale=tv_iterative iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 (all else held IDENTICAL to iter-2: tv_iterations=120, tv_lr=0.01, tv_clip_max=0.08, tv_decay=0.01, gd, fbp-init, val_n=214). NUMBERS: iter-1 SSIM 0.922979 hr 0.132941 RMSE 8.573e-4 (clip 0.05); iter-2 SSIM 0.923844 hr 0.205364 RMSE 7.857e-4 (clip 0.05->0.08) elapsed 928s. Trajectory: the clip bump moved hr +0.072 (0.133->0.205) and dropped RMSE 8.3% by un-truncating high-mu bone -- the clamp WAS the binding constraint (iter-2 falsifier 'hr<=0.133' NOT triggered). iter-2 clip_max=0.08 is now at the TOP of the solver search bound [0.03,0.08] so clip is exhausted as a lever. tv_lambda has been FROZEN at the solver default 0.001 for BOTH prior iters -- never probed -- and is the highest-value untouched knob (the classical data-vs-smoothness balance). FAILURE MODE: Mayo is real LOW-DOSE CT where the dominant error is photon/electronic noise, not under-sampling (2304 views is dense). At lambda=0.001 the data term dominates: SSIM barely moves between iters (recon is data-fit-dominated, leaving the LDCT noise floor in), and the iter-1->2 headroom gain came PURELY from un-truncating bone (clip), NOT from denoising. The regularizer is currently too WEAK to suppress LDCT noise. HYPOTHESIS: raising tv_lambda 0.001->0.003 strengthens the TV denoiser, suppressing residual LDCT noise so val_rmse drops below 7.857e-4 and hr rises above 0.205364; the RMSE-sensitive calibrated-headroom metric credits the lower noise floor. 3x is a bounded probe inside [0.0001,0.01] -- large enough to move the needle, small enough not to over-smooth in one shot. FALSIFIER: if hr <= 0.205 (no gain or regression) either side of lambda=0.003, TV is AT its regularization ceiling on Mayo (lambda=0.001 was already near-optimal) -- the lever is exhausted and the next probe would be tv_lr/tv_iterations for finer convergence, or accept ~0.92 SSIM / ~0.20 hr as the structural TV ceiling on real Mayo LDCT. BUDGET: tv_lambda is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~928s wall, ~272s margin under the 1200s hard 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-2 used 928/1200s, and lambda is the higher-value probe per the mandate. val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

rationale: wu_2015_trainable-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=1, lr=0.01, epochs=6, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42, rationale=wu_2015_trainable iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR: iter-1 = SSIM 0.8370 / hr 0.0508, 8 params (wu_n_bands=4, wu_n_outer=1, ep6, lr0.01), elapsed 335s. iter-2 = SSIM 0.8390 / hr 0.0337, 8 params (SAME but ep18), elapsed 866.6s. iter-1->iter-2 (epochs 6->18) was FLAT: val_ssim +0.0020 (within the +-0.001 noise band the iter-2 falsifier set), and hr actually FELL 0.0508->0.0337. Per-epoch train cost = (866.6-335)/(18-6) = 44.3 s/ep at n_bands=4. SLURM log confirms training converged (loss=0.00000 by ep1; band_scale already saturating to clamp by ep18) -- epochs is INERT, the falsifier for under-training FIRED. (2) FAILURE MODE: few-param tuned-FBP ceiling. Wu-trainable is a band-reweighted aliasing-free FBP + ONE soft-thresholded dense residual pass with NO image-domain CNN denoiser; it sits hr~0.04 just above the LD-FBP floor and epochs cannot move it. The OPEN question iter-2's falsifier handed to iter-3: is hr capacity-limited (too few frequency bands to separate signal from noise) or is the whole FBP-family structurally ceilinged regardless of capacity? (3) ONE KNOB: CAPACITY via wu_n_bands 4->6 (+2 frequency bands in the band-weighted aliasing-free FBP, line 198 band-loop). This is the iter-2 falsifier's prescribed lever ('iter-3 must add capacity, wu_n_bands up'). I deliberately pick wu_n_bands over wu_n_outer because (a) n_bands enriches the FBP frequency partition -- the exact structurally-FBP part the ceiling hypothesis is about; (b) it is BUDGET-SAFE: the band-loop (FFT-filter + back_project) scales LINEARLY with n_bands while the heavy dense-projector residual pass stays a single fixed pass at n_outer=1, vs wu_n_outer++ which DOUBLES that dominant cost; (c) wu_n_outer=1 is the campaign 'mandatory' hint, leave it. NEW PARAM COUNT: wu_n_bands+2+2*wu_n_outer = 6+2+2*1 = 10 trainable scalars (was 8). epochs held at the iter-1 anchor 6 (NOT a second knob -- iter-2 PROVED ep6 vs ep18 is a non-difference, 0.837 vs 0.839; reverting to ep6 restores the proven-equivalent baseline epoch budget so the wider 6-band bank fits the HARD 20-min wall with margin, isolating n_bands as the sole meaningful change). All else identical to iter-1/2: lr0.01, bs=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214(ALL L277), grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if iter-3 SSIM rises measurably above 0.839 (>+0.005 over the noise band) with hr>0.05, Wu-trainable was frequency-band-capacity-limited and more bands buy real headroom. FALSIFIER: if SSIM REGRESSES or stays FLAT (<=0.840, within noise of iter-1/2) at 6 bands, Wu-trainable is STRUCTURALLY FBP-ceilinged on Mayo regardless of capacity -- exactly matching the few-param-bilateral pattern THIS tick (dual_domain_bilateral_supervised img_n_bf 3->6: 0.9192->0.9057 REGRESSED; hammernik filters-up also regressed), i.e. capacity bumps DESTABILISE these few-param FBP-family denoisers rather than help. A regression would be the strong confirmation that the lever is the FBP family itself, not its band count. (5) HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score budget, sized via the ep6 anchor: worst-case (whole per-sample cost scaling with n_bands, which over-counts since the residual pass is fixed) ~1.5x the iter-1 per-epoch -> ~66 s/ep x 6 = ~396s train + ~120s for the 1.5x-wider 214-slice val pass ~= 520s, with the val FIGURE outside the budget and well under the 1800s SLURM kill. val = ALL 214 L277 slices (do NOT reduce); grad_clip=1.0; bs=1 + val_chunk=1 forced by per-sample-ps; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted; per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample model.proj/model.dense_proj swap; bg_target=truth; 321px detector-geometry FOV default (NO fov override). (6) no control return.

SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.919181 / hr 0.027984 in 254.3s @ ep8; iter-2 = SSIM 0.919155 / hr 0.028237 in 449.6s @ ep24 -- params_M 1.2e-05 (=12 params, proj_n_bf=1 img_n_bf=3). FLAT: ep8->24 moved SSIM 0.91918->0.91916 (-0.00003) and hr 0.02798->0.02824 (+0.0003, noise). (2) FAILURE MODE: NOT under-training -- the 3x-epoch iter-2 falsified the under-training hypothesis. The 12-param trainable bilateral is at a CAPACITY CEILING on the 2304-view Mayo FBP: only 4 scalar-sigma filters (1 proj + 3 img), too few DOF to push the calibrated RMSE-sensitive headroom past ~0.028 no matter how long they train. epochs is INERT (proven), so the lever is CAPACITY. This FIRES iter-2's own pre-registered falsifier ('if val_ssim stays <=0.81 still <FBP, the VN is smoothing-bound regardless of filter count, iter-3 must raise the DC weight vn_lambda_init'). MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-2 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB card (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise -- and a stronger DC step makes the clip MORE load-bearing).

rationale: r2gaussian-claude-agentic: val_n=214, gs_n_gaussians=512, gs_n_iter=400, gs_lr_pos=0.005, gs_lr_scale=0.01, gs_lr_amp=0.01, gs_lr_rot=0.01, gs_amp_init=0.01, gs_scale_init=0.04, gs_tv_weight=0.0001, gs_n_clip=0.05, gs_init_from_fbp=False, gs_outer_wall_s=1080, rationale=iter-2 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: gs_n_iter 150->400 (per-scene Adam steps; all other knobs held at iter-1). FAILURE MODE iter-1: SSIM 0.7383 < LD-FBP baseline 0.808 (hr=0), AND budget-starved -- the 1080s in-solver wall was HIT at sample 26/214 (log 765216: 42.4 s/scene = 282.9 ms/Adam-step, dominated by the dense 512^2 Gaussian rasterization + one 2304-view forward/backward proj). So iter-1 was BOTH under-fit per-scene AND covered only 12% of the 214 slices. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable in NUMBERS): the 0.7383 is per-scene UNDER-FIT, not a structural ceiling -- 2.67x more Adam steps will lift per-scene SSIM materially above 0.738 (the discarded 20260614 run reached SSIM 0.89-0.92 at gs_n_iter=6000 on val_n=20). FALSIFIER: if the ~9 scenes that finish at gs_n_iter=400 score <=0.76 SSIM (no material lift over 0.738), under-fit is REFUTED and 0.738 is a per-scene structural ceiling. BUDGET MATH: 282.9 ms/step x 400 steps = 113.2 s/scene; 1080s outer wall / 113.2 = ~9/214 scenes finish (well within the 20-min train+score budget; SLURM --time=00:30:00 has headroom, figure excluded). val_n stays 214 (NOT reduced); the per-scene loop self-truncates at the 1080s wall and scores whatever completed -- exactly as iter-1. This documents the R2Gaussian-lite quality-vs-coverage tradeoff on the 214-slice Mayo protocol: 6000 iters -> 0 scenes, 400 -> ~9, 150 -> 26 (none cover all 214 AND fit well -> structurally incompatible with the protocol, a real finding).

rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_unconstrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=5.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=0, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-2 search-20260619-01 UNCONSTRAINED diff-recon vs reused Mayo DDPM v4 ckpt (ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt). ONE KNOB: recon_eta 30.0 -> 5.0 (DPS soft-guidance gain DOWN). All else IDENTICAL to iter-1 (n_steps=25, init=fbp, recon_dcstep_every=0 so the hard-CG projection stays OFF -> pure soft DPS; recon_eta_clamp=false). iter-1 NUMBERS (eta=30): SSIM 0.3688, hr=0.0, PSNR 10.55, RMSE 0.01485, 868.65 s / 214 slices = 4.06 s/slice -- FAR BELOW the LD-FBP floor 0.8078 AND below its own FBP init, and below the constrained sibling's 0.3937. FAILURE MODE (shared with the constrained sibling's iter-2 diagnosis): eta is a dimensionless gain in the adaptively-normalized DPS step (step = (eta/||resid||)*grad, Chung 2023 eq.12); the literature/demo/breast default is 1.0, so eta=30 (a leftover discarded-614 boundary-metric hint) is a ~30x overshoot that, with recon_eta_clamp=false (no per-step displacement cap), blows the FBP-initialized iterate OFF-MANIFOLD every reverse step -> the recon is corrupted, not merely prior-dominated drift. DISTINCT FROM THE CONSTRAINED SIBLING (which is running eta 30->1.0 WITH hard-CG every=5): this unconstrained variant has recon_dcstep_every=0, i.e. NO hard-CG fidelity backstop, so the soft DPS gradient is its ONLY data-consistency mechanism -> it needs MORE guidance than the constrained sibling. I pick eta=5.0 (a clearly different magnitude than the sibling's 1.0) so the pair BRACKETS the soft-guidance response: constrained = gentle-soft (eta=1) + hard-CG; unconstrained = moderate-soft (eta=5) + no-CG. BUDGET: eta is a free scalar multiplier on the existing per-step gradient -- no extra forward/backward or projection calls -> per-slice cost stays ~4.06 s; 214 slices * 4.06 s = 869 s = 14.5 min < 20-min (1200 s) wall (~330 s headroom); n_steps unchanged so no budget risk. val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default). HYPOTHESIS: if I lower eta 30 -> 5, SSIM rises above the iter-1 0.3688 because the gentler-but-still-substantial soft DPS gradient keeps the FBP-initialized iterate on-manifold while still pulling toward the measurements (less off-manifold corruption). FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.37-0.5 (still << the 0.8078 LD-FBP floor) at eta=5 -- and the constrained sibling likewise fails to clear FBP at eta=1 -- then the DPS step size was NOT the issue: the Mayo v4 DDPM prior is mismatched to the rebinned-Mayo distribution under the 25-step low-T budget (mirrors the breast-DDPM hr=0 structural verdict: globally faithful but not conditionally faithful under DPS). iter-3 would then redirect to n_steps (longer DDIM trajectory) or accept an architectural prior-mismatch ceiling, not the guidance gain.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=4, n_iter=15, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, lr=0.001, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1080, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=dual_domain_n2i iter-2 (search-20260619-01, PER-IMAGE Noise2Inverse: warm-start pre-pass + per-scan Adam fit; NEVER amortized). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) iter-1: SSIM 0.8622, hr 0.0, PSNR 33.07 vs baseline_PSNR 34.08 (recon is BELOW the LD-FBP baseline), RMSE 1.11e-3, elapsed 971.99s (16.2 min). Measured from the [fit] log: per-scan fit loop = 214 scenes x 15 steps in 846.9s -> 0.264 s/per-scan-step = 3.96 s/scene; fixed overhead (1 warm-start epoch ~50s + dataset setup + scoring + figure ~75s) = 125.1s. (2) FAILURE MODE: hr=0, recon PSNR 33.07 < FBP 34.08 -> the per-scan fit is INIT-DOMINATED. At only 15 per-scan Adam steps the per-image recon has barely left the warm-start U-Net init, so the result is essentially the (1-epoch, under-trained) warm-start applied per scan -- below baseline. This is starvation of the INIT, not over-fit (the over-fit / lr-down regime is at n_iter 600-1200, far above here). (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 1->4 (n_iter=15, lr=1e-3, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, val_n=214, seed=42 ALL HELD). Why pretrain_epochs and not n_iter: the 214-scene budget HARD-CAPS n_iter -- at 0.264 s/step, a 19-min (1140s) total leaves 1015s of fit time -> 1015/(214*0.264) = 17.9 steps, so n_iter can only go 15->17 (+13%, too marginal to test). lr-down is wrong-signed (that lever is for the OVER-fit high-n_iter regime; here we are UNDER baseline). warm_start is LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE (confirmed cross-substrate) and the init is the anchor the 15-step fit refines, so DEEPENING the warm-start is the highest-leverage in-budget move. (4) HYPOTHESIS: pretrain_epochs 1->4 lifts SSIM above 0.8622 and ideally hr above 0 (PSNR above the 34.08 FBP baseline), because a deeper warm-start gives a better U-Net init that the fixed 15 per-scan steps refine from -- the recon stops being dominated by an under-trained 1-epoch init. FALSIFIER: if SSIM <= 0.8622 (no gain or regression), the warm-start init is NOT the binding constraint and per-image N2I is structurally FBP-bounded on dense 2304-view Mayo (half-view info loss > the per-image denoising gain) -> iter-3 documents the structural floor (NAF/ram class) rather than tuning further. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min, val=ALL 214): warm-start 4 epochs x ~50s = 200s (+150s vs iter-1) + fit loop UNCHANGED 846.9s + fixed setup/score/figure ~75s = 1121.9s = 18.7 min < 1200s/20-min hard wall (~78s margin). The fit loop is unchanged so its outer_wall_s=1080 in-solver backstop is unchanged; the warm-start is outside that wall and outside the budgeted [fit] timer. n_iter NOT raised (budget-capped). val_n=214 NOT reduced (protocol). PER-IMAGE structure unchanged. (6) no control return.

SIX-BOX. (1) iter-1 NUMBERS: SSIM 0.4729, hr 0.0, PSNR 18.55, baseline_PSNR 34.08; elapsed 1097s; naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2; SLURM [fit] log shows each scene fit only ~85-97 Adam steps (median 91) before the 5.0s per-scene wall, and the 18-min outer wall (1080s) was hit EXACTLY at scene 214 (elapsed 1082.5s). (2) FAILURE MODE: budget-starved per-scene INR fit. A NeRF-style coordinate-MLP wants hundreds-to-thousands of Adam steps to leave its water-mu init; ~91 steps/scene leaves the MLP barely moved -> SSIM 0.4729 well below the LD-FBP baseline. This is starvation, NOT (yet) the structural floor. (3) ONE KNOB: naf_hidden 128->64 (naf_layers=4, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_lr=1e-2, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, val_n=214 ALL UNCHANGED). 214-SCENE 20-MIN BUDGET MATH (measured): the entire budget is the per-scene fit loop (train_n=0); total = 214 x per_scene_s = 214 x 5.0s = 1070s ~= the 1080s/18-min outer wall, hit exactly at scene 214. I CANNOT raise per_scene_s (214 x wall is already full inside the 20-min compute budget). So to buy MORE Adam steps per scene at FIXED total budget I make each step CHEAPER: per-step cost ~0.055 s/step is the fixed 2304-view fan-beam forward+backward PLUS the tunable 512^2-coord MLP forward; halving width 128->64 cuts the dominant hidden x hidden matmuls ~4x, so each 5.0s scene should fit meaningfully more steps -> more useful optimization per scene within the SAME 214 x 1080s/18-min wall. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I shrink naf_hidden 128->64, I expect SSIM to rise above 0.4729 because the cheaper MLP buys more Adam steps per scene, letting the INR move further off its water-mu init within the same per-scene wall. FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.47 despite more steps, NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT), not merely starved. (5) HARD 20-min budget: 214-scene pass, naf_outer_wall_s=1080 (18 min) + naf_per_scene_s=5.0 (in-solver per-scene wall = the governor; naf_n_iter=3000 stays a high cap), val_n=214 (ALL L277 slices, NOT reduced), 321px detector-geometry FOV default (no fov= override). (6) no control return; the loop dispatches the next iter.

BUDGET: tv_clip_max is a ZERO marginal-compute knob -- identical iteration count (120) -> identical ~918s wall, ~282s margin under the 1200s 20-min budget preserved. tv_iterations deliberately NOT raised: iter-1 used 918/1200s, so more iters would risk the wall (the failure mode iter-1 flagged). val = ALL 214 L277 slices unchanged.

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=214, val_chunk=5, train_n=40, epochs=8, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=30, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_clip_max=0.05, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). PRIOR: iter-1 SSIM 0.2855 / hr 0.0, elapsed 321.5s — FAR below the classical (non-trained) tv_iterative sibling (SSIM 0.92298 / hr 0.133). FAILURE MODE (diagnosed iter-1): tv_K=10 unrolled steps is FAR too shallow vs classical TV (~120 iters) -> the recon is severely under-resolved; the 20 learnable scalars cannot compensate for missing depth. ONE KNOB CHANGED: tv_K 10 -> 30 (3x deeper unroll). All else identical to iter-1 (train_n=40, epochs=8, bs=1, lr=5e-3, val_n=214 ALL L277 slices, val_chunk=5, grad_clip=1.0, tv_step_init=0.01, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_clip_max=0.05). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00 with 10-min figure/IO headroom): iter-1 ran K=10 in 321.5s. Worst-case PURE-linear-in-K (assume all 321.5s is K-bound, fixed overhead=0): 32.15 s/K -> K=30 ~= 964s, ~20% under the 1200s wall. In reality a large slice of 321.5s is FIXED overhead (data load + 214-slice FBP precompute + per-ps probe ~60-120s), so the true K=30 cost is well under 964s. bs=1 holds only ONE K-step autograd graph at a time -> deeper K raises activation memory linearly but stays memory-safe on 16 GB (no OOM; cf. the hammernik bs=4 OOM). HYPOTHESIS: deeper unroll lifts SSIM toward the classical 0.92 band and clears baseline (hr>0), because 30 TV-GD steps resolve far more of the data-consistency + edge structure than 10 (closing the gap to classical 120 iters), and the learned per-iter step/lambda schedule adapts the balance across the deeper unroll. FALSIFIER: if SSIM/hr stay low at K=30, the limiter is NOT depth but the supervised-TV TRAINING (e.g. broken target/loss/optimisation), and iter-3 must check the training path (loss curve, learned step/lambda trajectory) rather than deepening further.

rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-2 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: vn_n_filters 16->24 (all else held: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). DIAGNOSIS from iter-1 SLURM log (765196): training CONVERGED by epoch 3 (loss 5.2e-6 ep3 -> 1.6e-6 ep7, asymptotically flat; wall tripped at ep7/14 in 1000s), and the VN settled at SSIM 0.805 BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). This is a CONVERGED-BUT-BAD basin, NOT under-training -- so epochs-up is INERT here (the proven epochs lever applied to genuinely under-trained trainers; this one has flat loss). lambda_t never moved from init (0.0023 across all 5 steps), so the tiny-DC + 16-filter regulariser converged to a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline. Per the brief conditional (epochs-up if budget allows, ELSE vn_n_filters or lr): training is converged AND near the wall -> capacity knob. vn_n_filters 16->24 (the solver default capacity) gives the learned filter bank enough degrees of freedom to learn an EDGE-PRESERVING regulariser instead of the smoothing it collapsed to with 16 filters. NOT touching lr (campaign has lr5e-4-optimal / 8e-4-worse on record). HYPOTHESIS: with 24 filters the regulariser can preserve structure rather than smooth, lifting val_ssim ABOVE the iter-1 0.805 and ideally to/above the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays <=0.81 (still <FBP), the VN family is structurally smoothing-bound at this DC weight regardless of filter count, and iter-3 must instead raise the DC weight (vn_lambda_init) so data-consistency dominates the regulariser. BUDGET: 24 filters ~1.3x the per-step RBF/conv cost; iter-1 did 7 ep in 1000s (143 s/ep) so expect ~5 ep in the 1000s wall -- still >3 (convergence point), so the converged-comparison is fair. Memory safe: vn_checkpoint=true + batch_size=2 keep N_k=24 (the solver memory-fitted default) within the card. max_train_s=1000 unchanged; total ~1300s under the 1800s SLURM kill.

rationale: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=3, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.0001, pretrain_epochs=48, pretrain_patience=48, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, max_train_s=960, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48 (4x); pretrain_patience tracked 12->48 so the early-stop never fires before the full 48 epochs (same disable-early-stop intent as iter-1, where patience==epochs). All else identical to iter-1 (k=3, unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0037, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42); only max_train_s 900->960 to admit the longer pretrain inside the wall. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 (val_psnr 21.24, val_rmse 0.00434) in elapsed_s=170.2 -- only ~14% of the 1200s (20-min) train+score budget used; pretrain_epochs=12. (2) FAILURE MODE: the pretrain-denoiser-then-data-consistency path UNDER-CONVERGES in the budget (same as v1, which was stuck at 0.441). The k=3 DC steps refine a denoiser that has not yet learned the Mayo image statistics; SSIM 0.455 is far below the end-to-end itnet_v3 sibling (0.896). With only 12 pretrain epochs at lr=1e-4 the denoiser is under-trained, and 170s/1200s proves the budget was almost entirely idle. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48, mirroring the SIBLING itnet (v1) iter-2 which raised pretrain_epochs 8->48 and jumped SSIM 0.441->0.593 (+0.15) under THIS campaign and metric -- the strongest just-proven signal that pretraining was the v1/v2 bottleneck. Chosen over lr-up (v3 is unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe v1 move) and over architecture knobs (k/unet_c) which would change the model not the convergence. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if pretrain_epochs 12->48, val_ssim rises substantially above 0.4554 (toward v1 iter-2's ~0.59, possibly the ~0.88-0.90 sibling band) because more pretraining lets the denoiser converge before the k=3 DC refinement, exactly as it did for v1. FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays flat (<=~0.47) at 48 epochs, the pretrain-DC architecture is CAPPED in this budget regardless of pretraining (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must move toward end-to-end unrolled training (the v3 recipe) or accept the pretrain-DC path is budget-limited. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 12 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 170s; the per-epoch pretrain cost over 200 stratified slices is the variable part and the 214-slice per-sample val + figure are roughly fixed. 4x the epochs is roughly 4x the small pretrain base plus the single fixed val/figure pass: est well under 600s, far below 1200s; max_train_s=960 is a 16-min HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged from iter-1): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override). residual_learning=False KEPT (the CONFIG default True double-applies the residual and collapses eval to ~0.34).

ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24 (3x). All else identical to iter-1 (proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3 -> 12 trainable params unchanged; 3*(proj_n_bf+img_n_bf)). SIX-BOX: (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.919 / hr 0.0279 in elapsed 254s -- only ~21% of the 1200s (20-min) budget used; 12-param bilateral, lr=5e-3. (2) FAILURE MODE: high SSIM but near-zero hr because the calibrated RMSE-sensitive headroom metric does not credit the bilateral's smoothing (campaign note: SSIM rewards the BF blur, headroom does not). Critically, with only 12 params at lr=5e-3 and 8 epochs the supervised-MSE loss -- which IS RMSE-sensitive, unlike SSIM -- has had little chance to drive the scalar sigmas to their RMSE-optimal (less-smoothing) values: the run is UNDER-TRAINED (254s/1200s). (3) ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24. JUSTIFICATION vs the other candidate (img_n_bf up): adding image-domain bilateral DEPTH at the current loose img_sr=0.02 would smooth MORE, which keeps SSIM high but does NOT lift the RMSE-driven hr (more blur is the wrong direction for headroom); whereas more epochs lets the MSE objective itself pull the sigmas toward the RMSE optimum AND uses the idle ~950s budget. epochs is the cleaner lever for the hr deficit. FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=~0.03 (flat) at 24 epochs, the 12-param bilateral is at its CAPACITY ceiling on the 2304-view Mayo FBP (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must instead add capacity (img_n_bf up) or attack the proj-domain over-smoothing (proj_sr) -- epochs is then exhausted. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 254s; per-step cost is dominated by the SHARED 2304-view FBP adjoint, not the 12 BF params, so 24 epochs ~= 3x train ~= 8 epochs*3 plus the single fixed val pass: est ~600-760s << 1200s. No headroom to raise epochs alone. LPD per-step cost is dominated by the projector forward+adjoint calls inside each unrolled iteration, so cut lpd_iters 5->3 (~40% fewer projector calls/sample) and REINVEST the freed budget into epochs 6->10. Everything else held EXACTLY at iter-1 (hidden=48, n_primal=5, n_dual=5, lr=5e-4 cosine, train_n=200, batch=1, val_chunk=1, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). HYP: a shallower-but-better-trained LPD clears the LD-FBP floor (hr>0) within 20 min. FALSIFIER: hr stays 0.000 (still at FBP floor) OR times out -> budget-bound projector-in-loop LPD cannot beat FBP on Mayo at this budget (documented ceiling) and the iters<->epochs trade is not the lever for iter-3.

rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=search-20260619-01 iter-2 OOM RESCUE of hammernik_2017. iter-1 (batch_size=4) was NOT a real recon: it CUDA-OOMed in the _rho_prime RBF-bump loop at elapsed_s=72.5 on a 16GB RTX5000 (val_score blank in results.tsv), recorded as 0.0. The (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF activation tensors held across 5 unrolled steps for autograd blew the card. SINGLE COHERENT memory-safety change for this rescue: batch_size 4->2, which halves every per-batch activation tensor in the bump loop -- the direct cause. NOTE: this hammernik_2017 solver is a PURE IMAGE-DOMAIN denoiser of the FBP (no projector in the unrolled loop) and does NOT read vn_checkpoint or vn_dc_norm (verified by grep over every cfg[...]/cfg.get(...) in the solver: only vn_T/vn_n_filters/vn_kernel/vn_n_bumps/vn_x_range/vn_*_init_std/vn_lambda_init/epochs/batch_size/lr/grad_clip/train_n/val_n/seed/max_train_s are consumed). Those two knobs belong to the SIBLING projector-in-loop hammernik_vn solver; passing them here would be silently ignored, so they are intentionally omitted -- the operative fix this solver honors is the batch halving (+ grad_clip=1.0 already present for VN-family NaN-skip stability). Budget: HARD 20-min train+score; val=ALL 214 L277 slices (321px detector-geometry FOV default, no fov= override; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps, bg_target=truth). batch=2 ~doubles steps/epoch, so epochs 40->14 (mirrors the sibling hammernik_vn iter-1 that scored 0.805 in 1296s); max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the binding constraint and leaves ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. capacity kept modest (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16). HYPOTHESIS: with batch halved the activation footprint drops ~2x, the OOM is avoided, hammernik_2017 produces its FIRST FINITE recon landing near/above the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor (sibling hammernik_vn hit 0.805) -- the first valid datapoint for this solver under the corrected metric.

rationale: dual_domain_supervised-claude-agentic: unet_c=16, lr=0.0001, epochs=20, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). ONE KNOB: epochs 8 -> 20 (everything else identical to iter-1: unet_c=16, lr=1e-4, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42). FAILURE MODE OBSERVED: iter-1 (SSIM 0.887976 / hr 0.275953, the campaign headroom LEADER) used only elapsed_s=418.58s (~7.0 min) of the HARD 20-min train+score budget -- i.e. ~35%% utilised, ~13 min of headroom UNSPENT. DD-UNet has no unrolled DC loop so it is cheap per step; at 8 epochs the supervised dual-domain U-Net is almost certainly UNDER-TRAINED at this budget (mirrors itnet_v3, which at iter-1 used only 12.3/20 min and whose lever was epochs-up; the discarded boundary-slice run also hinted epochs as the dominant lever for this solver). HYPOTHESIS: if I raise epochs 8->20 (everything else fixed), I expect val_ssim and headroom to RISE above the iter-1 baseline (hr>0.276), because the model is under-converged at 8 epochs and 2.5x more gradient steps will reduce the train MSE further without overfitting the L277 val (214-slice metric averages out per-slice noise). FALSIFIER: if hr does NOT exceed 0.276 (or DROPS) at epochs=20, the solver was already near its 8-epoch convergence basin -> epochs is NOT the lever and iter-3 should move to lambda_neg (1.0->0.1, discarded-run hint) or lr. BUDGET CHECK vs iter-1 measured time: iter-1 = 418.58s for 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure. Decompose ~140s fixed (data load + per-sample 214-slice val + figure I/O) + ~278s for 8 epochs (~35s/epoch). At epochs=20: ~140 + 20*35 = ~840s (~14 min) train+score; pessimistic (150s fixed + 40s/epoch) = ~950s (~15.8 min). rationale: diffusion_recon_dcstep_unconstrained_mayo_v4-claude-agentic: recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, recon_mode=dps, recon_sample_steps=25, recon_eta=30.0, recon_init=fbp, recon_eta_clamp=False, recon_dcstep_every=0, recon_dcstep_n_cg=3, recon_dcstep_warmup=5, recon_dcstep_relax=1.0, val_n=214, train_n=0, rationale=iter-1 search-20260619-01 UNCONSTRAINED diff-recon vs reused Mayo DDPM v4 ckpt (ddpm_mayo_unconstrained_v4.pt, ch=96, sees all 10 Wagner patients). CORRECTED metric: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV (default). SOFT DATA-CONSISTENCY ONLY: recon_dcstep_every=0 turns OFF the hard CG projection so data consistency is enforced ONLY by the per-step DPS adaptive-weight gradient (eta=30/||resid||, soft). This is the sole knob distinguishing this from the constrained sibling (which used recon_dcstep_every=5 hard-DC and scored SSIM 0.394 / hr 0 in 1019s). Budget: T=25 DPS steps with NO extra CG iters = strictly fewer proj-equivalents/slice than the constrained run, so it fits the 20-min wall with more headroom (constrained 214 slices ran 17 min). recon_dcstep_n_cg/warmup/relax are INERT here (gated on every>0). HYPOTHESIS: unconstrained soft-DC diffusion-recon lands at/below the ~0.84 LD-FBP floor on real rebinned Mayo, likely near the constrained 0.394 but possibly DIFFERENT because soft DC enforces measurements more weakly than the constrained hard CG projection (weaker fidelity -> prior dominates more, could drift further from anatomy).

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=1, n_iter=15, grad_clip=1.0, unet_c=16, lr=0.001, batch_size=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, outer_wall_s=1080, per_scene_s=None, seed=42, rationale=iter-1 baseline + feasibility for PER-IMAGE Noise2Inverse (warm-start pre-pass on train split + per-scan Adam fit on each L277 val scans own measurements; commit 1f4c3394 per-image rewrite -- NEVER amortized) under the CORRECTED Mayo metric (search-20260619-01: val=ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV). FAILURE MODE being managed: 214 independent per-scan Adam fits, each backpropping the 2304-view FBP adjoint, blow the 20-min wall at a naive n_iter (the discarded search-20260614-01 per-image iter-1 ran val_n=6 in 13.5 min @ n_iter=400 -> ~0.24 s/per-scan-step measured directly; 214 scenes is ~36x that scene count). MINIMAL-COST CONFIG: pretrain_epochs=1 (short warm-start; warm_start=True LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE per knob insights, do NOT disable), n_iter=15 per-scan steps (tiny), grad_clip=1.0 (mandatory -- 2304-view adjoint overflows otherwise), unet_c=16, lr=1e-3. BUDGET MATH (0.25 s/per-scan-step measured on Mayo 2304-view/512/c16): warm 200x1=50s + 214 scenes x 15 x 0.25 = 802s + ~60s overhead = ~912s (~15 min), 16.6 min even at +10% per-step -- inside the 20-min budget. outer_wall_s=1080 in-solver backstop on the per-image loop so even if timing drifts it stops cleanly and RECORDS (no SLURM timeout). HYPOTHESIS: per-image N2I is FBP-bounded on dense rebinned 2304-view Mayo (half-view info loss < full-view LD-FBP) AND budget-starved at 214 slices (only 15 per-scan steps each); expect hr~0 near the LD-FBP baseline -- this iter-1 establishes the datapoint under the corrected metric (analogous to the NAF/structural-negative class). val=ALL 214 L277 (protocol; do NOT reduce below 214).
